notes: Joint announcement of 2 August 2024 by the Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of Commerce, National Health Commission, Ministry of Emergency Management, General Administration of Customs and National Medical Products Administration, adding CBD to the Regulations on the Administration of Precursor Chemicals. It does not mention a personal-use allowance for travellers.
summary: Since 1 September 2024, China controls CBD as a Category II precursor chemical. The rules mention no personal allowance for travellers.

legal_source.name: Ministry of Emergency Management (joint announcement, 2 Aug 2024) — adding cannabidiol and six other substances to precursor-chemical control

limits.description: Since 1 September 2024, cannabidiol (CBD, CAS 13956-29-1) is managed as a Category II precursor chemical: its import and export follow China's rules for non-pharmaceutical precursor chemicals.

notes: Korea Customs says this applies even to medicines sold abroad or prescribed, if they contain controlled ingredients. Its one exception: carrying controlled medicine for your own treatment with prior approval from the Minister of Food and Drug Safety (apply through nedrug.mfds.go.kr).
summary: Banned: THC, CBD and cannabinol count as cannabis ingredients in Korea; bringing them in can mean life imprisonment or at least 5 years.

limits.description: Korea Customs lists cannabinol, tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and cannabidiol (CBD) as cannabis ingredients under the Narcotics Control Act; bringing them in is punishable by life imprisonment or at least 5 years.

legal_source.name: Korea Customs Service — Precautions for medicines containing narcotic ingredients (마약성분 함유 의약품 주의사항)

notes: Korea Customs says this applies even to medicines sold abroad or prescribed. Its one exception: carrying controlled medicine for your own treatment with prior approval from the Minister of Food and Drug Safety (apply through nedrug.mfds.go.kr).
summary: Banned: Korea treats CBD as a cannabis ingredient, even in medicines bought or prescribed abroad, unless you hold prior MFDS approval.

legal_source.name: Korea Customs Service — Precautions for medicines containing narcotic ingredients (마약성분 함유 의약품 주의사항)

limits.description: Korea Customs lists cannabidiol (CBD) with cannabinol and THC as cannabis ingredients under the Narcotics Control Act; bringing them in is punishable by life imprisonment or at least 5 years.

notes: National Assembly Resolution 173/2024/QH15 bans the production, trade, importation, possession, transportation and use of e-cigarettes and heated-tobacco products nationwide, in force since 1 January 2025; Vietnam Customs directed all customs departments (Official Letter No. 17/TCHQ-GSQL) to halt clearance of these products, and a December 2025 follow-up resolution closed related loopholes.
summary: Banned since 1 January 2025: e-cigarettes and heated-tobacco products can't be imported, carried, owned or used in Vietnam.

legal_source.name: WHO Viet Nam — National Assembly Resolution 173/2024/QH15 banning e-cigarettes and heated tobacco

_sources.claim: Vapes and related products are banned; you cannot buy vapes in Vietnam or bring them into the country
_sources.name: GOV.UK (FCDO) — Vietnam travel advice: Safety and security (updated 2026-09-21)

notes: ANVISA Resolution RDC 855/2024 explicitly prohibits the entry of electronic smoking devices into Brazil by travelers in any form, including in accompanied luggage, alongside a nationwide ban on their manufacture, import, sale, distribution, storage, transport and advertising.
summary: Banned: you can't bring e-cigarettes or other electronic smoking devices into Brazil in any form, including in your luggage.

legal_source.name: ANVISA RDC 855/2024, via the WHO FCTC Implementation Database

limits.description: Any drone weighing 250g or more must be registered with the FAA (DroneZone) before flying; recreational flyers must also pass the free TRUST knowledge test. Most drones must broadcast Remote ID; foreign-registered drones with Remote ID capability need to file a Notice of Identification with the FAA before flying in US airspace.

notes: This is a flight-operation requirement, not a customs import restriction — bringing a drone into the US isn't itself limited, but legally flying it (even recreationally) requires FAA registration completed in advance; there is no same-day tourist workaround described.

legal_source.name: FAA — Information for International UAS Operators in the United States

limits.description: A Flyer ID (theory test) is required for any drone 100g or heavier; an Operator ID is also required for drones 250g+ or 100-250g with a camera. The UK Civil Aviation Authority states it does not recognize overseas drone registrations or qualifications — visitors must obtain UK Flyer/Operator IDs before flying, regardless of what they hold at home.

notes: Confirmed directly from the CAA's own guidance page, which explicitly states foreign registrations aren't accepted — this is not just a formality for visitors, it's a real prerequisite to complete before arrival.
summary: Flying a drone of 100 g+ needs a UK Flyer ID; 250 g+ (or 100–250 g with a camera) also needs an Operator ID. Overseas registrations aren't accepted.

legal_source.name: UK Civil Aviation Authority — Registering to fly drones and model aircraft

limits.description: Registration with Japan's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) is mandatory for any drone weighing 100g or more, with no exemption for foreign visitors, in force since June 20, 2022.

notes: In practice, MLIT's online registration system requires a Japanese address and typically takes 7-10 business days to process, which makes same-trip tourist registration impractical without advance planning through a local agent or rental company.
summary: Drones of 100 g or more must be registered with MLIT before flying, including visitors' drones.

legal_source.name: MLIT (Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism) — Unmanned Aircraft Registration System

limits.description: Drones weighing more than 250g must be registered with the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA), and operators need a Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems Certificate plus a per-flight authorization before flying.

notes: NCAA's advisory circular page is real and reachable, but its detailed procedural text lives in a linked PDF that wasn't retrievable in this pass, so the 250g threshold and certificate process should be treated as the general shape of the rule rather than a word-for-word confirmed figure — undeclared drones risk being held in bonded customs storage pending the paperwork.
summary: Drones over 250 g must be registered with the NCAA, and you need a certificate plus authorisation for each flight.

legal_source.name: Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) — Unmanned Aircraft System Operations in Nigeria's Airspace (Guidance NCAA-GAD-AC-002)

limits.description: No registration, licence or accreditation is required for recreational drone flying in Australia at any weight, but standard operating conditions apply: fly no higher than 120m, stay at least 30m from other people, and drones 250g or heavier can't be flown within 5.5km of a controlled airport.

notes: Foreign-registered drones can't be separately registered in Australia, but that only matters for commercial operation — casual recreational tourist flying doesn't require it.
summary: No registration is needed for recreational flying, but stay below 120 m and 30 m from people, and away from controlled airports.

legal_source.name: Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) — Drone rules

limits.description: Importing a drone into Turkey involves registration in the civil aviation authority (SHGM) UAV registry and a Technical Compliance Certificate application filed with the Customs Directorate (SHT-İHA Instruction, Art. 6).

notes: SHGM's import page confirms the certificate procedure. Weight thresholds below which a drone is exempt, and the rules for foreign nationals flying in Turkey, weren't confirmed on an official page, so check with SHGM before you travel.
summary: Importing a drone involves SHGM registration and a customs technical compliance certificate. Check exemptions with SHGM before you travel.

legal_source.name: SHGM (Sivil Havacılık Genel Müdürlüğü / Turkish Directorate General of Civil Aviation) — İnsansız Hava Aracı İthali (UAV Import)

limits.description: Unmanned aircraft under 25kg are covered by Part 101 of New Zealand's civil aviation rules. Visitors may fly without registering, holding a licence, or a certificate, provided they follow Part 101's standard conditions: daylight only, within visual line of sight, yield to manned aircraft, get consent before flying over people or their property, and obtain ATC clearance in controlled airspace.

notes: New Zealand does not currently operate a drone registration scheme at all (one has been floated with no confirmed date) — this is a genuinely lighter-touch regime than most other destinations in this dataset.
summary: Visitors can fly drones under 25 kg without registration, following Part 101 rules: daylight, line of sight, consent over people.

legal_source.name: Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand — Part 101: Unmanned Aircraft and Rocket Operating Rules

limits.description: "民用无人驾驶航空器所有者应当依法进行实名登记" ("Owners of civil unmanned aircraft shall carry out real-name registration in accordance with the law") — Art. 10 of China's Interim Regulation on the Administration of Unmanned Aircraft Flights, in force since January 1, 2024. This real-name registration requirement applies to all civil drones regardless of weight.

notes: Bringing a personal consumer drone through Chinese customs is not itself restricted or specially declared. The registration requirement doesn't spell out a registration path for foreign operators.
summary: All civil drones must be registered under the owner's real name before flying, whatever their weight.

legal_source.name: State Council / Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC) — Interim Regulation on the Administration of Unmanned Aircraft Flights, Art. 10

limits.description: Nationally, Indonesia doesn't restrict bringing a drone through customs and doesn't require registration or a licence for recreational flying of Open Category drones under 25 kg, per Ministry of Transportation Regulation PM 37/2020.

notes: Regional rules may add requirements; we haven't confirmed any on an official page, so check with the local authority where you plan to fly.
summary: Nationally, recreational drones under 25 kg need no customs restriction, registration or licence under PM 37/2020.

legal_source.name: Peraturan Menteri Perhubungan RI No. PM 37 Tahun 2020 — Pengoperasian Pesawat Udara Tanpa Awak di Ruang Udara yang Dilayani Indonesia

limits.description: Drones over 250g must be registered through the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore's (CAAS) UA Portal: a S$25 registration label plus online registration, using Singpass or a UAPass account for foreign visitors, taking about 5 working days to process. The minimum age to register is 16. Drones of 250g or under are exempt from registration for basic recreational use.

notes: Confirmed directly from CAAS's own registration page, including the UAPass pathway specifically built for foreign visitors — apply before arrival, since the processing time doesn't support a same-day registration on landing.
summary: Drones over 250 g must be registered with CAAS (S$25 label, about 5 working days). Lighter drones are exempt for basic use.

legal_source.name: Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) — Registration / Deregistration (Unmanned Aircraft)

limits.description: Drones under 250g are exempt from registration. Drones of 250g or heavier must be registered through the Drone One-Stop portal, a Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport administrative system that lists a roughly 7-business-day processing time for aircraft registration.

notes: The Drone One-Stop portal itself was reachable and confirmed real in this pass (Korean government domains have historically been unreachable from this environment, so this is a genuine access breakthrough), but its registration process requires Korean-resident identity verification with no stated tourist exemption or workaround — in practice this blocks visitors from registering anything 250g or heavier. The specific 250g threshold comes from secondary sources, not the portal's own text.

legal_source.name: Drone One-Stop (드론원스톱 민원서비스) — Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport drone administrative portal

limits.description: Beef, mutton and pork are allowed only from Singapore Food Agency-approved source countries (the approved list includes Argentina, Australia, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Hungary, Ireland, Japan, Mexico, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Paraguay, Poland, Spain, Sweden, Uruguay and the USA for beef, with the exact list varying by meat type), capped at 5kg combined. Dairy and other processed food fall under the general non-commercial personal-food allowance of 5kg/5L/S$100 combined.

notes: The approved-country list differs by meat type (beef vs. pork vs. mutton) — check SFA's own list for the specific country and meat combination before assuming an origin is covered.
summary: Beef, mutton and pork only from SFA-approved countries, up to 5 kg. Other food falls under the 5 kg/5 L/S$100 allowance.

legal_source.name: Singapore Food Agency — List of Food & Food Products Allowed

limits.description: Fruit and vegetables are allowed from any country in a small, reasonable hand-carry quantity for personal consumption, within the general 5kg/5L/S$100 non-commercial food allowance.

notes: Importing at commercial scale without the required approvals carries a fine of up to S$10,000 and/or 3 years' imprisonment, per an Immigration & Checkpoints Authority enforcement release — that penalty applies to commercial-scale evasion, not an ordinary traveler's hand-carried snack.
summary: Small, reasonable amounts of fruit and vegetables for your own use, within the 5 kg/5 L/S$100 food allowance.

legal_source.name: Singapore Food Agency — General Rule to Bring Food into Singapore (Non-commercial)

limits.description: All animal products — meat, dairy, fish, honey, eggs, feathers, shells, wool, skins, bones — must be declared on arrival. Some (pork, trout, whole eggs) are banned outright; others are allowed only after inspection by Biosecurity New Zealand.

notes: Failing to declare, even accidentally, draws an instant NZD 400 infringement fine — New Zealand runs the strictest biosecurity enforcement in this dataset. A proposal to raise this to NZD 800 for high-risk items (meat, fresh fruit) was reported as of February 2026 but had not taken effect as law at the time of writing — don't assume it's in force.

legal_source.name: New Zealand Customs Service — What you can and can't bring (food and other risk items)

limits.description: Raw or artisanally-processed meat, cured meats, and non-industrialized milk/dairy are prohibited. Cheese, salami and doce de leite ARE allowed if in original manufacturer packaging with identifying labels — the packaging and labeling is what distinguishes an allowed item from a prohibited one.

notes: Per Portaria MAPA n° 872/2025: any animal product brought in without sanitary proof is treated as prohibited by default. Items that do require import authorization can be pre-declared via a MAPA-issued document before travel.
summary: Raw, cured or artisanal meat and unprocessed dairy are banned. Factory-packed, labelled cheese, salami and doce de leite are allowed.

legal_source.name: Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária (MAPA) — Viajantes e Bagagens (Portaria MAPA n° 872/2025)

notes: Fresh fruit, vegetables, seeds, seedlings, plants and flowers are prohibited without sanitary/phytosanitary proof, per Portaria MAPA n° 872/2025 — Brazil treats any plant product without that documentation as prohibited by default, and ordinary travelers don't carry it.
summary: Banned without sanitary or phytosanitary proof: fresh fruit, vegetables, seeds, seedlings, plants and flowers.

legal_source.name: Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária (MAPA) — Viajantes e Bagagens (Portaria MAPA n° 872/2025)

limits.description: Fully cooked/canned meat from disease-free countries needs no clearance. Processed-but-uncooked meat needs no SPS clearance but is capped at 10kg per passenger, with a veterinary health certificate or proof of purchase. Unprocessed meat requires an SPS Import Clearance for any quantity, however small.

notes: Per Bureau of Animal Industry Memorandum Circular 48, Series of 2021 — the cooked/canned-vs-uncooked-vs-unprocessed distinction is the whole rule; a canned corned beef and a raw steak are treated completely differently at the border.
summary: Fully cooked or canned meat needs no clearance; uncooked processed meat up to 10 kg with papers; raw meat needs SPS clearance.

legal_source.name: Bureau of Animal Industry (BAI) — Meat Products Import (Memorandum Circular 48, s. 2021)

limits.description: Bringing in fresh or semi-processed land-animal products, or fresh aquatic products, carried on your person: fine of VND 5–6 million and the products are destroyed (Art. 16(1)(b), 16(11)(b)). Not registering or declaring animal products subject to quarantine on import: VND 4–5 million (Art. 14(2)(a)).

notes: Decree 204/2026 took effect on 1 August 2026.
summary: Bringing in fresh or semi-processed meat, or fresh seafood, on your person: a VND 5–6 million fine, and the products are destroyed.

legal_source.name: Decree No. 204/2026/ND-CP on administrative penalties in veterinary medicine, Arts. 14 and 16 (Official Gazette, Công báo No. 346, 24 June 2026)

notes: Meat and poultry (beef, pork, lamb, chicken and processed forms like ham, sausage and jerky) and dairy (milk, cheese, butter) are barred from entry — even an in-flight meal containing these can't be carried off the plane.

legal_source.name: Korea Tourism Organization (official) — Animal/Plant Quarantine

notes: Fresh fruit and vegetables, cut flowers, seeds, saplings, bulbs, roots, and dried/fresh agricultural or medicinal-herb products are all barred from entry.
summary: Banned: fresh fruit and vegetables, cut flowers, seeds, saplings, bulbs, roots, and fresh or dried farm and medicinal-herb products.

legal_source.name: Korea Tourism Organization (official) — Animal/Plant Quarantine

limits.description: Plants for planting — seeds, bulbs, tubers, cuttings, grafts, rooted plants — are banned outright from non-EU countries in personal luggage. Fruit, vegetables, flowers and other plant products need a phytosanitary certificate issued in the country of origin, except for a short exempt list (pineapple, coconut, durian, banana, and dates, per Annex XI of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/2072), which need no certificate.

notes: Undocumented plant goods that don't fall on the exempt list are confiscated and destroyed at the EU external border, not just fined.

legal_source.name: European Commission — Your Europe: Taking animal products, food or plants with you in the EU

limits.description: Since 1 April 2026, France bans nicotine pouches and other oral nicotine products, such as nicotine beads, chewing gum, lozenges and liquids. The ban covers importing, transporting, possessing, buying and using them in France, so there's no traveller allowance. It applies to everyone, including travellers coming from other EU countries.

notes: Not covered by the ban: chewing tobacco, and nicotine medicines and medical devices used to quit smoking, such as pharmacy nicotine gum or inhalers. In December 2025 France's highest administrative court suspended only the parts of the decree on manufacturing, production and export; the ban on importing, possessing and using these products is in force. This is a French national rule, on top of the EU's customs allowances.

legal_source.name: Conseil d'État, order n° 509561 of 22 December 2025, quoting Décret n° 2025-898 du 5 septembre 2025 (art. R. 5132-45, code de la santé publique)

_sources.claim: Decree text: prohibition on national territory of production, manufacture, transport, import, export, possession, offer, transfer, acquisition and use of oral nicotine products; exemptions (chewing tobacco, medicines, medical devices, pharmaceutical raw materials, foodstuffs); in force 1 April 2026; suspension limited to manufacture, production and export
_sources.name: Conseil d'État, order n° 509561 of 22 December 2025, quoting Décret n° 2025-898 du 5 septembre 2025 (art. R. 5132-45, code de la santé publique)

_sources.claim: Ban from 1 April 2026 on pouches, beads, gums, lozenges, liquids; smoking-cessation medicines and devices and chewing tobacco excluded; import, possession and use ban in force
_sources.name: Service-Public.gouv.fr (Premier ministre) — Plusieurs produits à base de nicotine bientôt interdits en France (updated 12 March 2026)

limits.description: Don't bring it. Sweden has classified kratom (Mitragyna speciosa) as a narcotic since 11 March 2025, and the government says Swedish Customs can now stop it at the border. Its main active substance, mitragynine, was already a classified narcotic.

notes: This is a Swedish national rule, on top of the EU's customs allowances. It applies to everyone, including travellers from other EU countries where kratom is legal.

legal_source.name: Government of Sweden, Ministry of Health and Social Affairs — Regeringen narkotikaklassar kratom (press release, 10 February 2025)

limits.description: Kenya's Meat Control (Importation of Meat and Meat Products) Regulations require an import permit from the Director of Veterinary Services for meat or meat-product imports, via written application, a fee, and 24 hours' advance notice to the port of entry.

notes: This regulation reads as built for commercial importers, not obviously for a tourist carrying a personal quantity of cured meat or cheese — don't assume an ordinary traveler needs to apply for a Director-of-Veterinary-Services permit before a trip, but also don't assume they're exempt; Kenya's own page doesn't draw that line explicitly. Found via a search-snippet quote of the regulation text, not a direct fetch (403'd).
summary: Meat and meat products need an import permit from Kenya's Director of Veterinary Services, applied for in advance.

legal_source.name: Kenya Law — The Meat Control (Importation of Meat and Meat Products) Regulations

limits.description: All animal and fish product imports must carry quarantine documents from the country/region of origin, declared through Indonesia's "All Indonesia" app and inspected on arrival.

notes: Undocumented goods are confiscated and destroyed — enforcement was recently tightened specifically for goods originating from Malaysia amid Nipah-virus concerns, an example of how fast this can change by origin country.
summary: Animal and fish products need quarantine documents from the country of origin and must be declared on the All Indonesia app.

legal_source.name: Badan Karantina Indonesia (Indonesian Quarantine Agency) — Pengawasan Produk Hewan dan Tumbuhan Asal Luar Negeri

limits.description: All plant product imports must carry quarantine documents from the country/region of origin, declared through Indonesia's "All Indonesia" app and inspected on arrival.

notes: Undocumented goods are confiscated and destroyed.
summary: Declare all plant products in the All Indonesia app, with quarantine documents from the country of origin. Undocumented goods are destroyed.

legal_source.name: Badan Karantina Indonesia (Indonesian Quarantine Agency) — Pengawasan Produk Hewan dan Tumbuhan Asal Luar Negeri

limits.description: Decree No. 288/2025/ND-CP classifies drones by take-off weight in 5 tiers (under 0.25 kg, 0.25–under 2 kg, 2–under 25 kg, 25–under 150 kg, 150 kg and over). Import licences are issued by the provincial People's Committee after the Ministry of National Defence and the Ministry of Public Security give their views (Art. 6). Recreational drones under 0.25 kg flown outside no-fly and restricted zones are exempt from a flight permit, but must be notified to local military, police and air-traffic units if the flight affects military or civil flying (Art. 21). Flight-permit applications go in at least 7 days before the flight (Art. 22).

notes: The decree itself doesn't set fines or criminal penalties.
summary: Drones need a provincial import licence. Recreational drones under 250 g flown outside no-fly and restricted zones need no flight permit.

legal_source.name: Decree No. 288/2025/ND-CP on the management of unmanned aircraft and other aerial vehicles, Arts. 4, 6, 21–22 (Official Gazette, Công báo No. 1589+1590, 18 Nov 2025)

limits.description: Travellers aged 18 or over may bring one e-cigarette device they already use, plus one of: up to 200 heated-tobacco units, cartridges or e-liquid totalling no more than 30 ml, or up to 3 disposable e-cigarettes. There is no duty-free exemption for these goods.
limits.quantity: 1 device + 200 heated-tobacco units, or 30 ml, or 3 disposables

notes: Anything over these amounts is held in the customs baggage store and returned to you when you leave Turkey; if you don't collect it in time, customs destroys it. Commercial import of e-cigarettes is banned under Presidential Decision 2149 (2020), which left the traveller rule to the Ministry of Trade.
summary: Travellers 18+: one device in use, plus 200 heated-tobacco units, or 30 ml of liquid, or 3 disposables. Excess is held until you leave.

legal_source.name: Ministry of Trade, Directorate General of Customs — Circular 2020/7 on travellers entering with e-cigarettes and similar goods (31 March 2020)

_sources.claim: Traveller allowance, no exemption, excess held until departure and destroyed if not collected, transit rules; commercial import ban under Presidential Decision 2149
_sources.name: Ministry of Trade, Directorate General of Customs — Circular 2020/7 on travellers entering with e-cigarettes and similar goods (31 March 2020)

_sources.claim: Disposable allowance changed from 10 to 3
_sources.name: Ministry of Trade — Circular 2024/18 amending Circular 2020/7

transit.description: Passengers transiting Turkey by air don't enter the customs territory, so these limits don't apply to them. Transit passengers arriving by land or sea are treated like arriving travellers.

source.name: Ministry of Trade, Directorate General of Customs — Circular 2020/7 on travellers entering with e-cigarettes and similar goods (31 March 2020)

limits.description: Solid e-cigarettes: up to 140 units (batang) or 40 capsules (kapsul). Open-system e-liquid: up to 30ml. Closed-system e-liquid: up to 12ml. Crew-member allowances are lower than passenger allowances.

notes: Regulated under Peraturan Menteri Keuangan No. 34/PMK.04/2025 (amending PMK 203/2017).
summary: Limits: solid e-cigarettes up to 140 sticks or 40 capsules; open-system e-liquid up to 30 ml; closed-system e-liquid up to 12 ml.

legal_source.name: Direktorat Jenderal Bea dan Cukai (Indonesian Customs) — Barang Penumpang (Passenger Goods)

limits.description: Duty-free from age 19, as your one kind of duty-free tobacco: 20 ml of nicotine liquid with under 1% nicotine, or 200 heated-tobacco sticks, or 110 g of other e-cigarette types.

notes: Travellers under 19 (counted by year of birth) get no duty-free allowance for liquor or tobacco. Declare anything over the allowance: declaring it yourself takes 30% off the standard duty; if it is found undeclared, an extra 40% tax is added (60% if it happens twice or more within 2 years).
summary: Duty-free from age 19, one kind of tobacco only: 20 ml of nicotine liquid (under 1%), or 200 heated-tobacco sticks, or 110 g of other types.

legal_source.name: Korea Customs Service (English site) — Duty-Free Allowance for Travelers

_sources.claim: 20 ml nicotine liquid (under 1%); no allowance under 19; 30% reduction; 40%/60% penalty
_sources.name: Korea Customs Service (English site) — Duty-Free Allowance for Travelers

_sources.claim: Heated-tobacco sticks 200, other e-cigarette types 110 g; one kind of tobacco only
_sources.name: Korea Customs Service call centre FAQ — 면세범위를 초과하는 담배에 부과되는 세금 (tobacco allowances by type and taxes above them)

limits.description: RA 11900 ("Vaporized Nicotine and Non-Nicotine Products Regulation Act", signed 25 July 2022) legalized and regulates vape products under the DTI, but sets no statutory personal-import quantity cap. Customs applies an informal, discretionary "reasonable personal use" standard instead of a fixed number.

notes: This is the genuine, honest answer rather than a research gap — the law's full text is directly reachable and doesn't specify a quantity, and no DTI or Bureau of Customs page with a concrete traveler allowance was found either. Don't assume a specific number applies; expect discretion at the border.
summary: Vapes are legal and regulated; customs applies a reasonable personal-use standard rather than a fixed limit.

legal_source.name: Republic Act No. 11900 — Vaporized Nicotine and Non-Nicotine Products Regulation Act

limits.description: "Any person wishing to import fresh, chilled, frozen, salted, dried or smoked meat, other than that preserved by canning, is required to obtain from the national level veterinary authorities an import permit" — Ministerial Order on Animal Slaughtering and Meat Inspection, Art. 16, quoted directly. The rule is written in broad "any person" language with no traveler-specific exemption stated.

notes: This specific order doesn't address dairy products — no dairy-specific rule was found in this pass, so treat dairy as an open question rather than assuming it follows the same permit rule as meat.
summary: Fresh, chilled, frozen, salted, dried or smoked meat needs an import permit from the national veterinary authorities.

legal_source.name: Ministerial Order on Animal Slaughtering and Meat Inspection, Art. 16 (pursuant to Law n° 54/2008)

limits.description: "Any person entering Rwanda by air or by road with plants or plant products whether as accompanied or checked-in baggage, must declare such items to a competent employee at the point of entry" — Law on Plant Health Protection in Rwanda (2016), Art. 10, quoted directly. Art. 3 requires a license plus a phytosanitary certificate for plant/plant-product imports generally; Art. 4 allows exemptions via a Ministerial Order, but that order's exempt-items list wasn't read in this pass.

notes: The declaration duty applies broadly with no personal-quantity carve-out stated in the law itself.
summary: Declare all plants and plant products when you arrive; imports generally need a licence and a phytosanitary certificate.

legal_source.name: Law on Plant Health Protection in Rwanda (2016), Arts. 3, 4, 10

limits.description: Decree 214/2026/ND-CP, Art. 31: not declaring plants subject to quarantine carried in hand or checked baggage, VND 1–2 million (cl. 1); bringing them in without a plant quarantine import permit, VND 3–5 million (cl. 2); without a phytosanitary certificate from the exporting country, VND 10–20 million (cl. 4); with re-export or destruction as remedial measures (cl. 6).

summary: Plants subject to quarantine must be declared and need an import permit and a phytosanitary certificate; fines and re-export or destruction apply.

legal_source.name: Decree No. 214/2026/ND-CP on administrative penalties in cultivation, plant protection and plant quarantine, Art. 31 (government document portal)

limits.description: Travelers must file for a Plant Quarantine Clearance (PQC) prior to importation at the National Plant Quarantine Services Division (NPQSD) central office for personal-consumption plant, fruit and vegetable imports — a process explicitly distinct from the commercial import (SPSIC) pathway.

notes: The specific commodity categories this applies to (NPQSD's Category II/III/IV classification) weren't read in full in this pass — treat the PQC requirement itself as solid, but check NPQSD directly for whether a specific item needs it.
summary: File for a Plant Quarantine Clearance with NPQSD before bringing in plants, fruit or vegetables.

legal_source.name: DA-Bureau of Plant Industry, National Plant Quarantine Services Division (NPQSD) — Import Requirements

notes: "(生或熟)肉类(含脏器类)及其制品" (meat, raw or cooked, including organ meat and products thereof) and "动物源性乳及乳制品，包括生乳、巴氏杀菌乳、灭菌乳、调制乳、发酵乳，奶油、黄油、奶酪、炼乳等乳制品" (animal-origin dairy and dairy products, including raw milk, pasteurized milk, sterilized milk, flavored milk, fermented milk, cream, butter, cheese and condensed milk) are both listed as prohibited, quoted directly from Announcement No. 470's actual text.

limits.description: "税関限りの確認で通関が可能なカートリッジの数量は、用法用量からみて1ヶ月分" ("The quantity of cartridges that can clear customs with only a customs check is one month's supply, based on directions for use") — quoted directly from MHLW's own Q&A on pharmaceutical import procedures. Nicotine-containing e-cigarette cartridges and liquid are classified as pharmaceutical products under Japanese law (with the vaporizer device itself classified as a medical device), which is why this general pharmaceutical-import framework — the same one covering Japan's other medication rows in this dataset — applies to them.

notes: Above a 1-month supply, a Yakkan Shoumei (pharmaceutical import certificate) from a Regional Bureau of Health and Welfare is required, following the same process as Japan's other prescription/controlled-medication rows. Devices themselves (mods, pod systems, batteries) aren't restricted by this framework, though airline lithium-battery rules still apply.
summary: Nicotine e-cigarette cartridges are pharmaceuticals in Japan: up to one month's supply clears with a customs check only.

limits.description: In Japan, melatonin is on the health ministry's list of ingredients used only in medicines, so a melatonin supplement counts as a medicine at the border. Japan Customs lets you bring medicines for your own use without an import certificate (Yakkan Shoumei) up to 2 months' supply, or 1 month for prescription drugs. The ministry describes melatonin as a prescription medicine in Japan, so 1 month is the cautious reading (ours). Bringing more needs a Yakkan Shoumei in advance.
limits.quantity: Up to 1 month's supply (cautious reading) without a Yakkan Shoumei

notes: The ministry kept melatonin on its medicine-only list in 2023, citing its use as a prescription medicine in Japan and reported harm from supplements abroad.
summary: Melatonin is a medicine in Japan. Bring a small personal supply (1 month is the cautious reading); more needs a Yakkan Shoumei.

limits.description: Vaping products aren't mentioned anywhere on NZ Customs' own duty-free FAQ page, and aren't covered by the tobacco-specific concession (limited to 50 cigarettes, or 50g of cigars/tobacco/a mixture) — so they fall under the general goods concession instead: "You'll have to pay GST and duty if you bought more than NZ$700 in total" of duty-free items and related purchases.

notes: This corrects a previously-uncorroborated claim of a '3 month supply' vape-specific allowance, which doesn't appear anywhere on NZ Customs' actual site — the real rule is simpler: no vape-specific concession exists, so the general $700 threshold governs instead. Vaping products are regulated inside New Zealand (a disposable-vape sales ban, retailer age-verification rules) rather than at the border specifically.
summary: Vaping products fall under the general NZ$700 duty-free goods concession, not the tobacco allowance.

legal_source.name: New Zealand Customs Service — Duty-Free Shopping FAQs

limits.description: "Saudi law prohibits importation of the following products: weapons, alcohol, narcotics, pork and pork products..." — pork and pork products are absolutely prohibited, no exceptions. Separately, "the importation of the following products requires special approval by Saudi authorities: ... live animals ..." — live animals need advance authorization before import.

notes: Directly quoted from a U.S. government trade guide, not a Saudi government page itself (ZATCA's and SFDA's own prohibited-goods pages remain unreachable — 404s and unreadable scanned PDFs, a persistent block for this project on Saudi domains). This source is specific about pork and live animals but doesn't state a general rule for other meat or dairy products — don't assume non-pork meat or dairy is unrestricted just because it isn't named here; it simply wasn't confirmed either way in this pass.
summary: Pork and pork products are banned outright. Live animals need special approval in advance.

legal_source.name: U.S. International Trade Administration — Saudi Arabia: Prohibited and Restricted Imports

limits.description: "The importation of the following products requires special approval by Saudi authorities: agricultural seeds ..." — quoted directly. Seeds need advance authorization from Saudi authorities before import.

notes: This source confirms a special-approval requirement for agricultural seeds specifically — it doesn't separately address general fresh fruit and vegetables, so treat this row as covering seeds only, not a blanket fresh-produce rule, until a broader source is found.

legal_source.name: U.S. International Trade Administration — Saudi Arabia: Prohibited and Restricted Imports

limits.description: Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation Decree 1647 (1997) requires importers to apply to the General Organization for Veterinary Services (GOVS) for a permit before bringing in meat/animal products, with the epidemiological status of the country of origin taken into account; a granted permit is valid for 1 month and is renewable.

notes: The decree's own text and the USDA report describing it are both unreadable in this environment (scanned/binary PDFs) — this is drawn from the report's search-indexed summary rather than a directly read document, similar in tier to how this project has cited a USDA GAIN report for a different country's regulation elsewhere. The permit mechanism reads as built for commercial importers, similar to Kenya's meat-import regulation already in this dataset — no traveler/personal-quantity carve-out was found, so don't assume it applies the same way to a tourist's suitcase as to a commercial shipment. Egypt's National Food Safety Authority took over food-safety regulation generally in 2020 but still relies on GOVS for this specific import-permit mechanism.
summary: Meat and animal products need a permit from Egypt's General Organization for Veterinary Services before import.

legal_source.name: USDA FAS GAIN Report — FAIRS Country Report Annual, Cairo Egypt (EG2025-0025), re: Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation Decree 1647 (1997)

limits.description: "The medicines are allowed with a maximum of 6 bottles or three months' supply." Travelers must show proof the medicines are for personal use — a prescription, medical certificate or pharmacy label on the packaging — and may also be asked for a receipt or other proof of lawful purchase. Keep medicines in their original packaging.

notes: This is for ordinary, non-narcotic medication — medicines containing controlled substances follow a separate advance-permit process (see the dedicated controlled-medication entry for Korea).

limits.description: Anyone entering Korea with medicine containing a controlled substance needs a permit from the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) before arrival, whatever their nationality. You can bring only what you'll use during your stay, plus up to 5 days' extra for delays, and never more than a 90-day supply. Carry the medicine in your hand luggage.
limits.quantity: What you'll use during your stay, plus up to 5 days' extra, never more than 90 days' supply

notes: Medicine containing controlled substances can't be posted to Korea: MFDS says shipped medicine is seized and destroyed or returned. The permit is only for the person who takes the medicine, not family or friends. MFDS's guide doesn't say whether amphetamine products such as Adderall can be permitted, so ask MFDS before you travel with one. If you're not eligible, or you'll stay longer than 3 months, MFDS suggests asking your doctor about alternatives you can get prescribed in Korea. Korea Customs warns that bringing in medicine with controlled ingredients without that approval is punishable under the Narcotics Control Act, even if it was sold or prescribed abroad: life imprisonment or at least 5 years for ingredients such as codeine, morphine, oxycodone, methylphenidate (it names Ritalin, Concerta and Medikinet) and amphetamine isomers; up to 10 years or a fine of up to KRW 100 million for ingredients such as alprazolam, zolpidem, clonazepam and lorazepam.

procedure.title: Get an MFDS permit to bring in controlled medicine
procedure.authority: Narcotics Policy Division, Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS)
procedure.leadTime: At least 10 business days before you arrive. MFDS rejects applications made with less notice, and there's no way to speed it up.
documents: A clear, full-size copy of your passport.
Your flight booking, showing your name, flight number, arrival and departure dates and arrival airport.

A medical certificate or doctor's letter: hospital name, your name, the doctor's name and signature, the diagnosis and symptoms, each medicine's trade name and active ingredient, how to take it, the daily dose, the quantity prescribed and the issue date.
A valid prescription with your details, the issue date, the active ingredient, the dose and the quantity.
A drug export certificate from your home country's authorities, if your country issues one. If it doesn't, tick "Not available" on the application form.
Staying long-term for work or study: a supporting document such as an exchange-student or posting certificate.
steps: Gather the documents, in English or Korean. Anything in another language needs a notarised translation, sent with the original.
Apply online on MFDS's nedrug portal at least 10 business days before you arrive.
Ask only for what you'll use in Korea, plus up to 5 days' extra for delays. If you'll travel on to another country, attach that flight booking and you can include the medicine for that trip too.
MFDS emails or faxes the permit to you.
Carry the medicine in your hand luggage when you enter Korea.
procedure.atTheBorder: MFDS sends the permit to the agencies concerned, so carrying your copy isn't required, but it's useful to have. For questions about customs declarations, MFDS refers you to Korea Customs.

sources.name: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety — Guideline on permit to bring in narcotics for self-treatment, with FAQ (attachment to the MFDS notice)

transit.description: No permit is needed if you only change planes in Korea and don't go through immigration.

summary: Cough and cold medicines with dextromethorphan are controlled in Korea. Bring them only with prior approval from Korea's drug safety ministry.

limits.description: Korea Customs lists dextromethorphan as a psychotropic ingredient under the Narcotics Control Act: bringing it in without approval is punishable by up to 10 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 100 million. The exception is carrying medicine for your own treatment with prior approval from the Minister of Food and Drug Safety (apply through nedrug.mfds.go.kr; see Korea's controlled-medication entry).

notes: Korea Customs names NyQuil, DayQuil, Robitussin, Mucinex and Delsym among dextromethorphan medicines it has found at the border. Not every version of these brands contains dextromethorphan: check the active ingredients on your pack.

limits.description: "进出境人员随身携带的个人自用的少量药品，应当以自用、合理数量为限，并接受海关监管" ("Small quantities of medication for personal use carried by inbound/outbound persons shall be limited to self-use, reasonable quantities, and subject to customs supervision") — Art. 39, Measures for the Administration of Drug Import. There's no fixed numeric cap in the regulation itself; it's a "self-use, reasonable quantity" standard applied at customs' discretion.

notes: Narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances follow a separate, stricter framework — see the dedicated controlled-medication entry for China.
summary: Small, reasonable quantities for your own use are allowed, subject to customs checks. There's no fixed limit.

limits.description: "因治疗疾病需要，个人凭医疗机构出具的医疗诊断书、本人身份证明，可以携带单张处方最大用量以内的麻醉药品和第一类精神药品" ("For treatment of illness, an individual, upon presenting a medical diagnosis certificate issued by a medical institution and personal ID, may carry narcotic drugs and Category I psychotropic substances not exceeding the maximum quantity of a single prescription") — Art. 44, Regulations on the Administration of Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (State Council Order No. 442). Without this documentation, expect much stricter scrutiny. Healthcare workers carrying such drugs for medical duty need a certificate from a provincial drug-supervision department instead.

notes: Which specific common Western medications (e.g. Adderall/amphetamine-class ADHD stimulants) count as "Category I psychotropic substances" under China's own drug schedule was not independently confirmed against a named-substance list in this pass — Amphetamine and methylphenidate are psychotropic substances on the UN's international list, but we haven't read China's own category list, so don't assume which category a specific drug is in.
summary: Narcotic and Category I psychotropic medicines: up to one prescription's maximum, with a medical diagnosis certificate and ID.

limits.description: "A passenger aged 18 or above is allowed to bring into Hong Kong, for his own use, 1 litre of alcoholic liquor with an alcoholic strength above 30% by volume" duty-free (measured at 20℃). Hong Kong ID card holders must have spent 24 hours or more outside Hong Kong to claim it.

notes: The 1-litre concession only matters for spirits: Hong Kong's duty schedule charges 0% on wine and on liquor other than wine of 30% ABV or less, so beer and wine aren't dutiable. Passengers who fail to declare, or make a false or incomplete declaration of, dutiable goods above the concession are liable to prosecution under the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance.
summary: Travellers 18+ can bring 1 litre of alcohol over 30% duty-free; HK ID holders must have been away 24 hours or more.

legal_source.name: Hong Kong Customs and Excise Department — Duty-free Concessions

summary: Duty-free from age 18: only 19 cigarettes, or 1 cigar (or 25 g of cigars), or 25 g of other tobacco. A pack of 20 is over the limit.

limits.description: "A passenger aged 18 or above is allowed to bring into Hong Kong, for his own use, the following quantity of tobacco products exempted from duty: 19 cigarettes; or 1 cigar or 25 grams of cigars; or 25 grams of other manufactured tobacco."
limits.quantity: 19 cigarettes, or 1 cigar / 25 g of cigars, or 25 g other manufactured tobacco

notes: One of the smallest tobacco allowances in the world — a single pack of 20 exceeds it. Passengers who fail to declare excess dutiable goods are liable to prosecution. E-cigarettes and heated tobacco are a separate, stricter matter: see the e-cigarettes entry for Hong Kong.

legal_source.name: Hong Kong Customs and Excise Department — Duty-free Concessions

limits.description: Anyone arriving at a specified control point with currency and bearer negotiable instruments totalling "more than HKD120,000" must "make a declaration to a Customs officer, using the Red Channel." The threshold applies in any currency (declare in the original currency, e.g. USD 20,000); an adult accompanying a child under 16 declares on the child's behalf.

notes: Maximum penalty for failing to declare or disclose is a fine of HK$500,000 and two years' imprisonment. A first-time breach can be settled by paying HK$2,000 if the traveller has no prior money-laundering or terrorist-financing conviction and the money isn't suspected crime proceeds. Hong Kong has no currency import cap, only this declaration duty.
summary: Declare cash and bearer instruments totalling more than HKD 120,000 in the Red Channel.

legal_source.name: Hong Kong Customs and Excise Department — Currency and Bearer Negotiable Instruments

limits.description: "No person may import an alternative smoking product by way of parcels, cargoes, and bringing in by incoming travellers." The ban covers e-cigarettes, heated tobacco (heat sticks), herbal cigarettes and their accessories, regardless of quantity or personal use. Import penalty on summary conviction: a fine of HK$500,000 and two years' imprisonment.

notes: Since 30 April 2026 it is also an offence to possess a specified alternative smoking product in a public place: a HK$3,000 fixed penalty for small non-commercial quantities (up to 5 capsules / 5 mL / 100 heat sticks / 100 rolls), or a fine of up to HK$10,000 on conviction, and up to HK$50,000 and six months' imprisonment for larger quantities. Don't pack a vape, pods or heat sticks for Hong Kong, even in checked luggage; the Tobacco and Alcohol Control Office page doesn't describe any personal-use exception.
summary: Banned: travellers can't bring in e-cigarettes, heated tobacco or herbal cigarettes. Fines up to HK$500,000 and 2 years' prison.

legal_source.name: Tobacco and Alcohol Control Office, Department of Health — Ban on Alternative Smoking Products

limits.description: Cannabis is a dangerous drug under the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance (Cap. 134). Hong Kong Customs "reminds members of the public not to bring any cannabis products or products containing CBD into Hong Kong." Trafficking (including importing and exporting) carries a maximum penalty of a fine of HK$5 million and life imprisonment; possession and consumption carry up to HK$1 million and seven years' imprisonment.

notes: There is no medical or personal-use exception for travellers, and no THC threshold. Edibles, oils, vape cartridges and food or drinks containing cannabis all count.
summary: Banned: cannabis and CBD are dangerous drugs in Hong Kong, with up to life imprisonment for importing.

legal_source.name: Hong Kong Customs and Excise Department — Customs takes strict enforcement action to control cannabidiol (CBD) from February 1 (press release)

limits.description: "CBD has been listed as a dangerous drug under the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance (DDO)" since 1 February 2023. "Importation of products (including food or drinks) containing CBD into Hong Kong is prohibited unless the relevant provisions in the DDO are complied with," with no exemption based on concentration. Maximum penalty for trafficking (including import): HK$5 million and life imprisonment; for possession or consumption: HK$1 million and seven years.

notes: Unlike most of the world, Hong Kong treats even zero-THC CBD as a dangerous drug: skin care, edible oils and supplements containing CBD are all covered. The Narcotics Division adds that CBD products can contain trace THC and that CBD can decompose into THC in storage.
summary: Banned since 1 February 2023: CBD is a dangerous drug in Hong Kong, in any concentration, including food and drinks.

legal_source.name: Narcotics Division, Security Bureau — Legislative Control of Cannabidiol (CBD)

limits.description: "Pharmaceutical products and medicines imported in the personal baggage of a person entering Hong Kong and which are accompanied by him and in a reasonable quantity for his personal use may be exempted from licensing requirement." No numeric day-supply cap is published; "reasonable quantity for personal use" is the test.

notes: This exemption covers ordinary medicines. Medicines containing dangerous drugs (see the controlled-medication entry for Hong Kong) need prior written approval from the Drug Office. Medicines containing endangered-species ingredients need separate approval under species-protection law.
summary: Medicine you carry yourself, in a reasonable quantity for personal use, is exempt from licensing.

legal_source.name: Drug Office, Department of Health — Frequently Asked Questions (medicines carried by visitors)

transit.description: If your medicine contains a dangerous drug under Hong Kong law, you need the Drug Office's prior written approval even if you're only transiting through Hong Kong. The Drug Office doesn't state a transit rule for other medicines.

limits.description: A visitor wishing to bring medicine containing dangerous drugs (as defined under the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, Cap. 134) must obtain "prior written approval issued by the Drug Office of the Department of Health", supported by a certification letter from the local doctor giving the doctor's name and medical registration number, clinic details, the patient's name and address, and the drug name, dosage form, strength and total quantity, with the doctor's original signature. Processing normally takes 10 working days; carry both the letter and the approval while travelling.

notes: Customs' list of dangerous drugs includes opium, morphine, heroin, cannabis, cocaine and amphetamines, so amphetamine-based ADHD medication such as Adderall falls in this approval regime (an inference from that list). Which other prescription drugs (for example specific benzodiazepines or methylphenidate brands) are scheduled under Cap. 134 was not confirmed in this pass — ask the Drug Office (tel. +852 2572 2068, pharmgeneral@dh.gov.hk) before travelling with them.
summary: Medicine containing dangerous drugs needs prior written approval from the Drug Office; allow 10 working days.
