notes: "Marijuana is still listed under the Category two narcotics in accordance with 'Narcotics Hazard Prevention Act' in Taiwan." "Offenders of manufacturing, transporting, selling, cultivating, transferring, possessing or taking Category two narcotics are subject to life imprisonment or a minimum ten-year fixed-term imprisonment, and may also be subject to a fine of no more than fifteen million New Taiwan dollars." There is no recreational or medical exception, and Taiwanese customs authorities have specifically warned travelers not to bring in cannabis products even from countries where cannabis is legal (e.g. Thailand).
summary: Banned: marijuana is a Category 2 narcotic in Taiwan; possessing or transporting it can mean life or at least 10 years in prison.

legal_source.name: Taipei Customs, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan) — Taipei Customs Urges the Public Not to Import Cannabis and Its Related Products

limits.description: CBD is regulated in Taiwan as an ordinary drug, and no CBD medicine is approved for sale there. To bring a CBD medicine prescribed to you, you must first apply to the Taiwan FDA for a special personal import under the Regulations on Management of Medicament Samples and Gifts, and show that permit at customs. A product with more than 10 ppm THC counts as a Category 2 narcotic, the same as cannabis.

notes: Without the TFDA permit at clearance, Customs treats a CBD product as an illegal import of a prohibited drug under the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act: up to 10 years' imprisonment and a fine of up to NT$100 million. The page doesn't address products sold as cosmetics or food.
summary: Only with a TFDA special-import permit for a CBD medicine prescribed to you, applied for before travel. Over 10 ppm THC it counts as a narcotic.

legal_source.name: Taichung Customs, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan) — Importing CBD Products Without Permission Can Lead to Penalties

limits.description: "Almost all kinds of meat products made from land animals are NOT permitted to carry into Taiwan." The fine for bringing in undeclared meat products generally is "NTD 10,000 to NTD 1,000,000" under infectious-disease-prevention law. Pork specifically is under a further, harsher rule: Taiwan has "banned the import of all kinds of pork products from ASF [African Swine Fever]-infected areas," with a first-time violation fined at a flat "NTD 200,000, regardless of nationality," rising toward NT$1 million for repeat violations; foreign nationals who don't pay the fine at the border are repatriated.

notes: Taiwan detected its first-ever domestic African Swine Fever case in October 2025, so enforcement has tightened further. This page does not separately address dairy products — treat dairy as an open question rather than assuming it's exempt from the general animal-product restriction.
summary: Almost all meat products are banned. Pork from ASF-affected areas carries a NT$200,000 fine for a first offence.

legal_source.name: Taipei Customs, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan) — What Food Products Can I Bring Into Taiwan (African Swine Fever Prevention)

limits.description: "禁止攜帶活植物及其生鮮產品" ("Bringing live plants and fresh plant products is prohibited"), with an exception only for items that separately comply with plant quarantine regulations. Fresh fruit specifically has been banned from passenger baggage since 1 October 1998.

notes: Dried plant products (dried flowers, dried vegetables, dried fruit, dried spices) and some seeds (e.g. vegetable and spice seeds) can be brought in after declaring at the quarantine counter and passing inspection — this is a genuinely different, less strict rule than for fresh produce, so don't assume all plant matter is banned. The customs page mentions "severe penalties" for violations without stating an exact fine figure.
summary: Banned: live plants and fresh plant products, including fresh fruit, unless they meet plant quarantine rules.

legal_source.name: Taipei Customs, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan) — Agricultural, Livestock, Fishery Products and Food

limits.description: "Passengers are NOT allowed to carry e-cigarettes and e-liquids into Taiwan." Violators "may be fined between NT$50,000 and NT$5 million according to Paragraph 1 of Article 15 and Paragraph 2 of Article 26 of the Tobacco Hazards Prevention Act."

notes: Taiwan's amended Tobacco Hazards Prevention Act (in force since 22 March 2023) fully bans e-cigarettes — manufacture, import, sale and use — and separately regulates heated-tobacco products like IQOS, which are also barred for travelers to bring in. If merely transiting Taiwan for another destination, devices can be declared and deposited at the bonded luggage counter for collection on departure, rather than being confiscated outright.
summary: Banned: e-cigarettes and e-liquids can't be brought into Taiwan. Fines range from NT$50,000 to NT$5 million.

legal_source.name: Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan) — Are Passengers Allowed to Bring Electronic Cigarettes into Taiwan?

transit.description: On a short layover in Taiwan, declare e-cigarettes and e-liquids at the red "Goods to Declare" counter when you arrive. Customs keeps them at the bonded luggage counter, and you collect them when you leave.

source.name: Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan) — Are Passengers Allowed to Bring Electronic Cigarettes into Taiwan?

limits.description: "Firearms (including shotguns, air guns, fishing guns, etc.), ammunition (including artillery shells, bullets, bombs, explosives, etc.), and knives referred to in the Act Governing the Control of Guns, Ammunition and Knives" are prohibited, "excluding those permitted by competent authorities."

notes: Taiwan has extremely strict, near-total gun control — private possession of firearms and ammunition is generally illegal outright, and there is no realistic tourist path to authorization.
summary: Banned: firearms, air guns, ammunition and controlled knives, unless authorised by the competent authorities.

legal_source.name: Kaohsiung Customs, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan) — Prohibited Articles

limits.description: Drones with a maximum take-off weight over 250g must be registered with Taiwan's Civil Aeronautics Administration (CAA) before flying (Regulations of Drone, Art. 6(1)); drones under 250g owned by an individual are exempt from registration. Foreign nationals bringing their own drone face an extra step regardless of weight class for anything requiring registration: under Art. 38(1)-(2), they must submit documents to the CAA and can only fly "after CAA's certification," and a foreign visitor holding valid drone credentials from their home country can get that certification valid for "a maximum of six month after the date of issuance."

notes: A tourist bringing a small recreational drone under 250g can fly without registering it at all, regardless of nationality. Operating a heavier drone (2-15kg with navigation systems, or anything over 15kg) also needs a Remote Pilot License with age/testing requirements on top of the registration/certification above — a materially higher bar than just registering the aircraft.
summary: Drones over 250 g must be registered with the CAA, and foreign visitors need CAA certification before flying.

legal_source.name: Laws & Regulations Database of the Republic of China (Taiwan) — Regulations of Drone, Arts. 6, 38

limits.description: Duty-free per traveler 17 or older: 1 litre of spirits over 22% ABV, OR 2 litres of beverages up to 22% ABV and sparkling wines, PLUS (separately) 2 litres of still wine and 10 litres of beer. "No relief for alcohol and tobacco shall be granted to travellers under 17 years old."
limits.quantity: 1L spirits >22% ABV, or 2L ≤22% ABV/sparkling; plus 2L still wine and 10L beer

notes: Quoted directly from the General Directorate of Customs' own traveler page. Amounts above this are dutiable and must be declared.
summary: Travellers 17+: 1 litre of spirits or 2 litres up to 22%, plus 2 litres of still wine and 10 litres of beer.

legal_source.name: General Directorate of Customs (Republic of Albania) — Tobacco, alcoholic drinks and coffee

limits.description: Duty-free per traveler 17 or older: "200 cigarette" or "100 cigarillos" or "50 cigars" or "250 grams of smoking tobacco." "No relief for alcohol and tobacco shall be granted to travellers under 17 years old."
limits.quantity: 200 cigarettes, or 100 cigarillos, or 50 cigars, or 250g smoking tobacco

notes: Quoted directly from the General Directorate of Customs' own traveler page. E-cigarettes are a separate matter — see the e-cigarettes entry for Albania, which has no equivalent explicit traveler allowance.

legal_source.name: General Directorate of Customs (Republic of Albania) — Tobacco, alcoholic drinks and coffee

limits.description: Travelers entering or leaving Albania "are obliged to declare the amounts in cash, any type of instrument negotiable of the holder, metals or precious stones, valuables and antiques, starting from the amount of 10,000 euros or its equivalent in other currencies."

notes: Quoted directly from the General Directorate of Customs' own traveler page. The threshold covers precious metals/stones and antiques as well as cash and negotiable instruments, and applies on both entry and exit.
summary: Declare cash, bearer instruments, precious metals or valuables worth €10,000 or more.

legal_source.name: General Directorate of Customs (Republic of Albania) — Cash Declaration

limits.description: Foreign travelers may carry limited quantities of medicines for personal use if: (1) not for promotion/marketing, (2) they complete a written statement that the medication is for personal use and provide the prescribing doctor's contact details (Albanian or foreign), deposited with customs at the entry point, and (3) the amount covers no more than 2 months of treatment, justified by the accompanying doctor's prescription showing the daily dose. Non-residents' quantity should match the length of their stay in Albania.
limits.quantity: Up to a 2-month supply, with prescription and a customs declaration

notes: Quoted/paraphrased directly from the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs' own page on this exact topic. This is the general-medicine rule; medicines classed as narcotic or psychotropic substances are far more restricted — see the controlled-medication entry for Albania.
summary: Up to 2 months' supply, with a prescription and a signed personal-use statement deposited with customs.

legal_source.name: Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs (Republic of Albania) — Travel of foreign citizens with drugs for minimal consumption

items: The doctor's prescription, showing the daily dose (covering no more than 2 months of treatment)
A written statement that the medication is for personal use, deposited with customs at entry
The prescribing doctor's contact details

source.name: Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs (Republic of Albania) — Travel of foreign citizens with drugs for minimal consumption

limits.description: The Customs Authority's own prohibitions page states plainly: "It is prohibited the import, export, transit of narcotics and psychotropic substances" — a criminal offense under Albanian Criminal Law — and this explicitly extends to "plants, narcotic medicaments and psychotropic substances of natural or synthetic nature, their materials and their preparations", with reference to Law No. 7975 (26.07.1995) "On the narcotic medicines and psychotropic substances".

notes: Unlike ordinary medication, the Customs Authority's page describing narcotics/psychotropic substances states a blanket import prohibition with no traveler or personal-medical-use exception mentioned. No personal-use carve-out was found on an Albanian government page — do not assume one applies. If you take a medication that is a controlled substance in your home country, verify directly with the Albanian Embassy before travelling.
summary: Banned: Albanian Customs prohibits the import of narcotic and psychotropic medicines.

legal_source.name: General Directorate of Customs (Republic of Albania) — Narcotics and Psychotropic Substances and human trafficking

transit.description: Albania's customs authority prohibits the transit of narcotics and psychotropic substances, as well as their import and export.

source.name: General Directorate of Customs (Republic of Albania) — Narcotics and Psychotropic Substances and human trafficking

limits.description: Covered by the same blanket ban as other narcotics: "It is prohibited the import, export, transit of narcotics and psychotropic substances," which explicitly extends to "plants, narcotic medicaments and psychotropic substances of natural or synthetic nature." A criminal offense under Albanian Criminal Law.

notes: Albania has had major real-world cannabis cultivation and trafficking enforcement over the past decade, and the Customs Authority's page names no medical or personal-use exception for travelers. There is no THC threshold or de minimis carve-out stated.
summary: Banned: Albania prohibits importing narcotics, including narcotic plants; it's a criminal offence with no personal-use exception.

legal_source.name: General Directorate of Customs (Republic of Albania) — Narcotics and Psychotropic Substances and human trafficking

transit.description: Albania's customs authority prohibits the transit of narcotics and psychotropic substances, including plants, as well as their import and export.

source.name: General Directorate of Customs (Republic of Albania) — Narcotics and Psychotropic Substances and human trafficking

limits.description: "Foreign citizens have the right to enter with firearms in the territory of the Republic of Albania only after they are equipped with a temporary authorization issued by the competent body of the State Police." Category B and C weapons separately require State Police authorization for trading, import/export, hunting, or sporting purposes.

notes: You cannot simply bring a firearm into Albania — a prior temporary authorization from the State Police is required. The Customs Authority's page doesn't address bladed weapons, air weapons, or self-defense items specifically, so don't assume those are unregulated; the U.S. ITA country guide separately confirms "special import provisions are enforced for strategic sectors such as weapons, munitions."
summary: Foreigners can bring firearms only with a temporary authorisation from the State Police.

legal_source.name: General Directorate of Customs (Republic of Albania) — Weapons

limits.description: Duty-free from outside the EU: 1 litre of drinks over 22% alcohol (or undenatured ethyl alcohol of 80% vol. and over), or 2 litres of drinks not over 22%; plus 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer. Travellers under 17 get no alcohol allowance. Anything over the allowance must be declared in the red channel.
limits.quantity: 1 L spirits or 2 L ≤22%; 4 L still wine; 16 L beer

notes: These are the EU allowances for travellers entering the EU from a non-EU country (Your Europe, europa.eu), which Cyprus Customs lists as its general allowances. Other goods (not alcohol/tobacco) are duty-free up to €430 per person (€175 for travellers under 15, per Cyprus Customs).
summary: From outside the EU: 1 litre over 22% or 2 litres up to 22%, plus 4 litres of wine and 16 litres of beer.

legal_source.name: Cyprus Customs & Excise Department — Travellers: dual channel system and general allowances

limits.description: Duty-free from outside the EU: 200 cigarettes, or 100 cigarillos (max. 3 g each), or 50 cigars, or 250 g of smoking tobacco. Travellers under 17 get no tobacco allowance. Declare anything over the allowance in the red channel.

notes: Cyprus applies the EU's higher tobacco limit (Your Europe lists the countries applying the lower limit; Cyprus is not among them).

legal_source.name: Cyprus Customs & Excise Department — Travellers: dual channel system and general allowances

limits.description: Anyone entering or leaving Cyprus with €10,000 or more in cash (or the equivalent in other currencies or bearer instruments such as traveller's cheques), or gold worth €10,000 or more, must declare it in writing to Customs at the point of entry or exit. Failing to declare is an offence: the cash or gold is seized and you can be fined up to €50,000.

notes: Cyprus Customs' page (last updated 2020) still cites the repealed Regulation (EC) 1889/2005; the current EU rule is Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 (EC DG TAXUD), which keeps the €10,000 threshold and defines cash as banknotes and coins, bearer negotiable instruments, gold coins of at least 90% gold and gold bars/nuggets of at least 99.5% gold. Cyprus' page also applies the declaration to travel to/from other EU member states (national Law 53(I)/2009).
summary: Declare €10,000 or more in cash or gold in writing. Undeclared amounts are seized, with fines up to €50,000.

legal_source.name: Cyprus Customs & Excise Department — Cash Control; cross-checked with European Commission DG TAXUD — EU Cash Controls (Regulation (EU) 2018/1672)

limits.description: You cannot bring meat, milk or their products (including cheese) into Cyprus from outside the EU in your luggage. Fish, honey and powdered infant milk follow separate, more lenient EU limits.

notes: Conflict between sources, recorded per AGENTS.md §3.8: the EU rule (Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2122, directly applicable) allows fish up to 20 kg and honey up to 2 kg, but Cyprus Customs' restrictions list says meat, fish and cheese need authorisation from the Director of Veterinary Services and honey needs a Veterinary Services licence. The list may refer to commercial imports; if you plan to bring fish or honey, check with Cyprus Veterinary Services first. These rules don't apply to products coming from other EU countries, Andorra, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, San Marino or Switzerland.
summary: Banned from outside the EU: meat, milk and their products, including cheese. Fish and honey have separate limits; check with Veterinary Services first.

legal_source.name: European Commission — Personal imports of animal products (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2122)

limits.description: Under EU rules you can bring, from outside the EU: fishery products up to 20 kg (or one fish, if heavier); other animal products such as honey up to 2 kg; and powdered infant milk, infant food or special foods needed for medical reasons up to 2 kg, if they don't need refrigeration before opening and are in unbroken branded packaging.

notes: Conflict between sources, recorded per AGENTS.md §3.8: the EU rule (Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2122, directly applicable) allows fish up to 20 kg and honey up to 2 kg, but Cyprus Customs' restrictions list says meat, fish and cheese need authorisation from the Director of Veterinary Services and honey needs a Veterinary Services licence. The list may refer to commercial imports; if you plan to bring fish or honey, check with Cyprus Veterinary Services first. These rules don't apply to products coming from other EU countries, Andorra, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, San Marino or Switzerland.
summary: From outside the EU: fish up to 20 kg, honey up to 2 kg, and infant or medical food up to 2 kg.

legal_source.name: European Commission — Personal imports of animal products (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2122)

limits.description: Plants, fruit, vegetables and cut flowers from outside the EU may not be brought in your luggage unless accompanied by a phytosanitary certificate. No certificate is needed for pineapples, coconuts, durians, bananas and dates. Cyprus Customs additionally requires a licence from the Director of the Department of Agriculture and a phytosanitary inspection for flowers and plants.

summary: From outside the EU, plants, fruit, vegetables and cut flowers need a phytosanitary certificate. Pineapples, coconuts, durians, bananas and dates don't.

legal_source.name: European Commission — Trade in plants & plant products from non-EU countries (passengers' luggage; Regulation (EU) 2019/2072)

notes: Cyprus Customs lists narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances and other controlled pharmaceuticals among goods whose importation is prohibited.
summary: Banned: narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances are prohibited imports into Cyprus.

legal_source.name: Cyprus Customs & Excise Department — Prohibitions & restrictions (passengers)

limits.description: Cyprus Customs lists cannabis derivatives under prohibited imports — explicitly including oil and flour from cannabis seeds, cannabis contained in foods and beverages, and other cannabis derivatives. The competent authority is the Chief of Police.

notes: Customs states its lists are not exhaustive and refers enquiries to the competent authority (Chief of Police). The list doesn't name CBD (cannabidiol); our reading is that CBD oils and other CBD products made from cannabis are 'cannabis derivatives' under it.
summary: Banned: Cyprus Customs lists cannabis derivatives, including oils and foods, as prohibited imports.

legal_source.name: Cyprus Customs & Excise Department — Prohibitions & restrictions (passengers)

limits.description: Visitors can bring small quantities of internationally controlled medicines (narcotics or psychotropics) for their own treatment only with a permit issued by Cyprus's Pharmaceutical Services (Ministry of Health). The application asks for your passport number, arrival and departure dates, and each drug's name, form, strength, daily dose and prescribed quantity, and must include a copy of your prescription showing the doctor's name, address, phone/fax and licence number. Without a permit, Customs treats narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances and other controlled pharmaceuticals as prohibited imports.

notes: Apply to Pharmaceutical Services before you travel (phscentral@phs.moh.gov.cy). The Application Form for Import for Personal Use is linked from the source page.
summary: Controlled medicines need a permit from Cyprus's Pharmaceutical Services; without one, customs treats them as prohibited.

legal_source.name: Cyprus Ministry of Health, Pharmaceutical Services — Narcotics and Psychotropics (permits for visitors carrying controlled medicines)

procedure.title: Get a permit from Cyprus's Pharmaceutical Services
documents: The application form for patients carrying controlled drugs: your name, postal address, phone, email or fax, place and date of birth, passport or ID number, arrival and departure dates, and each drug's name, form, strength, daily dose and prescribed quantity, signed by you.
A copy of the prescription showing the doctor's name, address, phone and fax number and licence number.
steps: Download the application form from the Pharmaceutical Services page and fill it in.
Attach a copy of your prescription.

Send it to Pharmaceutical Services before you travel. The page lists phscentral@phs.moh.gov.cy, tel. +357 22 608620 and fax +357 22 608649 as contacts, but gives no lead time or processing time, so apply early.

limits.description: Bringing a drone is not restricted, but flying it is regulated under EU (EASA) rules. Visitors from outside the EU who have not flown in another EU country before must register as an operator with Cyprus's Department of Civil Aviation (age 18+, €15, VISA card only) and attach the operator registration number to every drone. Registration is needed if the drone weighs more than 250 g, or has a camera or other sensor able to capture personal data. Non-EU residents also need an A1/A3 remote pilot certificate (online training and exam, €15, valid 5 years) — not required for a C0 drone under 250 g. No flying in no-fly zones and keep at least 8 km from airports and heliports.

notes: If you already registered in another EU country (where you first flew), do not register again in Cyprus.
summary: Drones over 250 g, or with a camera, need operator registration with Cyprus's Civil Aviation Department; visitors also need an A1/A3 certificate.

legal_source.name: Cyprus Department of Civil Aviation — Unmanned Aircraft (drones.gov.cy)

limits.description: Prohibited: flick knives and daggers; automatic firearms, long-barrel semi-automatic or repeating firearms, ammunition, military explosive devices and projectile launchers (per Law 113(I)/2004, First Annex). Restricted — permit from the Chief of Police needed: air rifles up to 4.5 mm, hunting guns taking no more than two cartridges per loading, sporting pistols, sporting archery equipment and handcuffs. Explosives, hunting cartridges and fireworks need an import licence from the Inspector of Mines.

notes: Customs states its lists are not exhaustive; contact Customs Headquarters or the Police before travelling with any weapon.
summary: Flick knives, daggers and automatic firearms are banned; air rifles and hunting guns need a Chief of Police permit.

legal_source.name: Cyprus Customs & Excise Department — Prohibitions & restrictions (passengers)

limits.description: Tourists: two regular-size bottles of wine and one and a half litres of spirits, duty-free.

notes: Sri Lanka Customs' passenger guide lists the tourist exemption as 'Two regular-size bottles of wine and one and a half liters of spirits' (plus toilet water up to a quarter litre and a small quantity of perfume and souvenirs up to US$250). The Passenger Services Directorate page states the foreigner limit as '1½ litres' of alcoholic beverages (residents 2½ litres) and adds that 'All liquor should either be purchased from Sri Lanka Duty Free shops or brought from abroad on the day of arrival. Liquor sent as Unaccompanied Baggage will not be allowed free of duty.' Excess is taxed at normal rates.

legal_source.name: Travellers — Passenger Guide, Sri Lanka Customs

notes: Sri Lanka Customs' Passenger Services Directorate page states: 'Cigarettes, Cigars, Beedies and Snuff are not allowed to be imported to Sri Lanka as personal baggage (accompanied or unaccompanied).' There is no duty-free tobacco allowance — the tourist exemption in the Customs passenger guide lists only clothing, wine/spirits, toilet water, perfume and souvenirs. Other forms of tobacco (e.g. loose pipe tobacco) are not named on the page; e-cigarettes are not addressed (see unverified).

legal_source.name: Passenger Services Directorate — Sri Lanka Customs

limits.description: Declare to Customs on arrival if you bring in more than US$15,000 (or equivalent); you receive a currency declaration receipt. Declare when leaving if you take out more than US$10,000.

notes: Sri Lanka Customs: 'Any passenger may bring in or take out any amount of money in the form of currency' provided it is legally acquired. Bringing in currency exceeding US$15,000 or equivalent 'Must be declared to Customs — a currency declaration receipt will be issued'. Taking out currency exceeding US$10,000 must be declared. If you want to take previously brought-in currency back out, declare it on arrival even if it is below US$15,000. The Customs passenger guide also lists foreign currencies, gold jewellery and gems among items to declare to the Customs Arrival officer. GOV.UK separately notes you cannot transfer money without an exchange control permit from the Central Bank of Sri Lanka.

legal_source.name: Passenger Services Directorate — Sri Lanka Customs

limits.description: Personal medicine without prior NMRA approval: the quantity needed for your stay or up to 90 days, whichever is less, in the original container (or labelled with name, strength and instructions); show medical records or prescription when asked.
limits.quantity: length of stay, max 90 days' supply

notes: NMRA 'Instruction for travelers': 'A person travelling to Sri Lanka can carry medicine for his personal use, without prior approval of the NMRA' under these conditions: the quantity of any single medicine for the duration of the stay or up to ninety days, whichever is less; prior NMRA approval for quantities exceeding a 90-day requirement; medicine 'administered through intramuscular or intravenous route is not permitted'; 'The medicine specified in Schedule III is not permitted'; original container or appropriate labelling; medical records or prescription produced when necessary. For medicines not registered/available in Sri Lanka, NMRA issues a personal user Letter of Authorization (prescription, request letter, ID copy, prescriber-signed form; max 100 doses; no fee; email pa5@nmra.gov.lk). The NMRA page carries no visible date.
summary: Up to 90 days' supply, or your stay if shorter, in original containers. Show your prescription if asked.

legal_source.name: Bringing Personal Medicines into Sri Lanka — National Medicines Regulatory Authority (NMRA)

notes: NMRA's traveller instruction excludes 'The medicine specified in Schedule III' from the personal-medicine allowance ('not permitted'), and any quantity above a 90-day supply needs prior NMRA approval. Separately, the Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs Ordinance (s.54A(c)) makes it an offence, 'except as permitted by ... the provisions of this Chapter or a licence of the Director', to import any dangerous drug listed in Part III of the Third Schedule above the amounts set there, with severe penalties (s.54A(a) sets death or life imprisonment for manufacturing heroin, cocaine, morphine or opium). We could not find the content of NMRA's 'Schedule III' on an official page, so we cannot say which specific drugs (e.g. ADHD stimulants, benzodiazepines, codeine) are excluded. If your medicine is a narcotic or psychotropic, contact NMRA (info@nmra.gov.lk, +94 11 2698896) before travel. Sources: NMRA traveller page (https://www.nmra.gov.lk/announcements/bringing-personal-medicines-into-sri-lanka) and the Ordinance text published by NMRA (https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/666d0695ca3ba7fa496a5068/66d0118a99a826f61299405c_podd_drugs_ordinance_06.pdf).
summary: Medicines in NMRA's Schedule III aren't permitted, and more than a 90-day supply needs NMRA approval first.

legal_source.name: Bringing Personal Medicines into Sri Lanka — National Medicines Regulatory Authority (NMRA)

notes: NMRA's traveller instruction states: 'The medicine administered through intramuscular or intravenous route is not permitted' under the no-prior-approval personal allowance. The page does not mention subcutaneous injectables (such as insulin pens or GLP-1 pens) either way, so this row does not cover them — ask NMRA (info@nmra.gov.lk) before travelling with any injectable. For an intramuscular/intravenous medicine you need, NMRA's personal-user Letter of Authorization route (prescription, request letter, ID, prescriber-signed form) is the official channel, though the page does not say explicitly that it applies to travellers' IM/IV medicines.

legal_source.name: Bringing Personal Medicines into Sri Lanka — National Medicines Regulatory Authority (NMRA)

notes: Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs Ordinance s.28: 'No poppy plant, coca plant, or hemp plant [Cannabis sativa L], or seeds, pods, leaves, flowers, or any part of any such plant or any preparation thereof, shall be imported or brought into or exported from Sri Lanka.' s.29 bans possession or use of hemp resin and preparations 'commonly known as bhang, hashish or ganja' except as licensed (s.30 exempts licensed galenical preparations and hemp rope/fibre). GOV.UK travel advice: 'Illegal drugs, including cannabis, carry severe penalties' and 'You should expect a long jail sentence and heavy fines', including in transit; airports use technology to detect illegal items. Medical-cannabis prescriptions from other countries are not recognised anywhere in these sources. CBD products are not specifically addressed by an official traveller page (see unverified).
summary: Banned: no part of the hemp (cannabis) plant, or any preparation of it, may be brought into Sri Lanka.

legal_source.name: Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs Ordinance (as amended to Act No. 26 of 1986), ss. 28–29 — text published by NMRA

transit.description: UK government travel advice says to expect a long jail sentence and heavy fines for possessing, using or smuggling illegal drugs, including cannabis, "including when transiting through the airport". Sri Lanka's airports scan transit passengers' baggage too.

source.name: GOV.UK (Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office) — Sri Lanka travel advice: safety and security

notes: Sri Lanka Customs: 'All fruits including Apples, Grapes, Mangoes, Peaches, Kiwi etc. are not allowed to be imported by air in personal baggage. All such items will be referred to the plant quarantine unit at BIA and will be destroyed.' Plants need a permit from the Department of Agriculture – Plant Quarantine Unit (Katunayake) obtained before leaving for Sri Lanka, plus a phytosanitary certificate from the exporting country; otherwise they are detained. Some plants (Orchids, Adeniums, Hoya, Ixora) are allowed with a licence; Anthurium, palm, Ficus, citrus and conifer families are not allowed. 'Any part of a plant (including fresh or dried fruits, leaves, seeds, twigs, roots etc.)' is restricted without prior approval. The page does not specifically address vegetables or processed plant foods.

legal_source.name: Passenger Services Directorate — Sri Lanka Customs

notes: CAASL: the drone import procedure (MOD, CAASL, TRCSL and Import & Export Control Department no-objections) 'is exclusively relevant to drones imported into the country for permanent use. For drones brought in by visiting tourists for temporary use within the country, there is no need to adhere to the outlined process. Instead, for such visitors, please proceed to submit a request for flying approval through our online portal.' So you may bring a drone for temporary use, but you need CAASL flying approval before flying. CAASL lists minimum third-party liability cover by take-off weight (not required at 0.25 kg or below; LKR 100,000 above 0.25–0.9 kg; LKR 400,000 above 0.9–4 kg; higher above). Its model-aircraft procedure starts with a mandatory security clearance from the Ministry of Defence. CAASL publishes restricted and archaeological area maps. GOV.UK advises not to fly drones near military bases, government buildings or VIP vehicles.

legal_source.name: Drones — Civil Aviation Authority of Sri Lanka (CAASL)

limits.description: Declare gemstones to Customs on arrival (US$200 service fee per person). Only bona fide personal gold jewellery in reasonable quantity; no ingots, gold biscuits or rough/unfinished jewellery.

notes: Sri Lanka Customs: 'If a person wishes to import gemstones as passenger baggage, it should be declared to Customs. A service fee of USD 200 will be charged per person.' Exporting gemstones must go through the National Gem and Jewellery Authority; otherwise it is treated as smuggling. 'Only bona fide personal jewellery in reasonable quantity is allowed to be imported and exported'; 'Rough and unfinished jewellery, Ingots and Gold Biscuits are not allowed to be imported or exported as passenger baggage.' Antiques over 100 years old need Department of Archaeology approval to export.

legal_source.name: Passenger Services Directorate — Sri Lanka Customs

limits.description: Travellers over 18 may bring up to 3 litres of liquor duty-free without declaring it.

notes: SUNAT lists 'Licor (3 litros)' among goods you need not declare, 'solo para mayores de 18 años'. Anything over that must be declared on the Declaración Jurada de Equipaje (red channel) and is taxed. Undeclared goods are seized; to recover them you pay the duties plus a fine of 50% of their customs value (SUNAT). Goods beyond the free list are taxed at a single 12% rate up to US$1,000 per trip (max US$3,000 per calendar year, per SUNAT's 'Ingresar equipaje al país' page); above that, normal import duties apply. Separately, foreign-made drinks labelled 'pisco' are prohibited (see pisco row).
summary: Duty-free from age 18: up to 3 litres of liquor without declaring it. Declare anything more; it is taxed. Foreign-made "pisco" is banned.

legal_source.name: Bienes y artículos no obligados a declarar y que puedes ingresar libres de impuestos al Perú — SUNAT (gob.pe, last changed 14 Jan 2024)

limits.description: Travellers over 18: 20 packs of cigarettes, or 50 cigars, or 250 g of cut/loose smoking tobacco, duty-free.

notes: SUNAT's duty-free list: 'Cajetillas de cigarrillos (20 unidades). Cigarros puros (50 unidades) o tabaco picado o en hierbas para fumar (250 gramos)', only for over-18s. SUNAT does not state the number of cigarettes per pack. The 2017 SUNAT declaration form shows the three as alternatives ('o'). Undeclared goods are seized; to recover them you pay the duties plus a fine of 50% of their customs value (SUNAT). Goods beyond the free list are taxed at a single 12% rate up to US$1,000 per trip (max US$3,000 per calendar year, per SUNAT's 'Ingresar equipaje al país' page); above that, normal import duties apply.
summary: Duty-free for over-18s: 20 packs of cigarettes, or 50 cigars, or 250 g of loose smoking tobacco.

legal_source.name: Bienes y artículos no obligados a declarar y que puedes ingresar libres de impuestos al Perú — SUNAT (gob.pe, last changed 14 Jan 2024)

limits.description: Declare cash and/or negotiable bearer instruments over US$10,000 (or equivalent). Carrying more than US$30,000 into or out of Peru is not allowed.

notes: SUNAT: travellers entering or leaving must declare cash and/or negotiable financial instruments (traveller's cheques, bearer cheques and promissory notes, etc.) 'siempre que sea un monto mayor a US$ 10 000,00'; 'No está permitido ingresar o salir del país llevando dinero y/o instrumentos financieros negociables por más de US$ 30 000,00'. Use the Declaración Jurada de Equipaje plus the cash declaration form at the SUNAT (Aduanas) office after baggage claim. Failing to declare or declaring falsely means temporary retention of the full amount and a penalty of 30% of the undeclared value. Conflict: SUNAT's 'Bienes o artículos que debes declarar' page (gob.pe/15285) writes the ceiling as 'S/ 30,000.00' (soles); the dedicated cash page and SUNAT's declaration form both say US$30,000, which we treat as correct.
summary: Declare cash or bearer instruments over US$10,000. Carrying more than US$30,000 into or out of Peru is not allowed.

legal_source.name: Ingresar y salir con dinero del país — SUNAT (gob.pe, last changed 23 Sep 2019)

limits.description: Medicines for your own personal use are treated as personal effects and need not be declared.

notes: SUNAT lists 'medicamentos' among personal-use goods that pay no tax and need no baggage declaration 'siempre que sean para tu uso personal'. Medical aids and equipment you need (wheelchairs, crutches, blood-pressure, temperature or glucose meters, etc.) are also free in a 'reasonable quantity for your trip'. Narcotic and psychotropic medicines are controlled substances in Peru (DIGEMID, D.S. 023-2001-SA) and are NOT covered by this row — see the controlled-medication entry. SUNAT does not state a prescription requirement for accompanied baggage; carrying your prescription is prudent but not a cited rule.
summary: Medicines for your own use count as personal effects: no tax and no declaration. Narcotic and psychotropic medicines are controlled separately.

legal_source.name: Bienes y artículos no obligados a declarar y que puedes ingresar libres de impuestos al Perú — SUNAT (gob.pe, last changed 14 Jan 2024)

limits.description: Injectable medicines for personal use (e.g. insulin) and the medical devices you need (e.g. glucose meters) can be brought as personal goods.

notes: Same SUNAT rule as personal medication: 'medicamentos' for personal use need no declaration, and 'medios auxiliares y equipos necesarios para tu control médico... medidores de presión arterial, temperatura o glucosa, entre otros' are allowed in a quantity 'razonable para tu viaje' for travellers who are ill or disabled. SUNAT does not name specific brands (so no GLP-1 brand names are listed here) and does not mention syringes or needles specifically.
summary: Injectable medicines for personal use, such as insulin, and devices like glucose meters can come in as personal goods, in a reasonable quantity.

legal_source.name: Bienes y artículos no obligados a declarar y que puedes ingresar libres de impuestos al Perú — SUNAT (gob.pe, last changed 14 Jan 2024)

limits.description: Must declare. Packed and labelled, from countries without sanitary restrictions: pasteurised dairy up to 5 kg (or one cheese up to 10 kg); sausages/cured meats up to 10 kg; canned ready meals up to 2 kg; honey, royal jelly, pollen up to 1 kg. ALL pork products are banned.
limits.quantity: Dairy 5 kg; sausages 10 kg; canned 2 kg; honey 1 kg; no pork

notes: SENASA: every passenger must declare animal products on the passenger declaration and take meats, sausages, eggs and other livestock products to the SENASA office in the arrivals hall; 'SOLO PODRÁN INGRESAR AL PERÚ LOS PRODUCTOS DECLARADOS Y AUTORIZADOS POR EL SENASA'. Without an import permit, allowed only if properly packed and labelled and not from countries with sanitary restrictions: 'Lácteos pasteurizados hasta 5 kg. o un solo molde de queso no mayor a 10 kg', 'Embutidos (excepto de origen porcino) hasta 10 Kg', 'Comida rápida enlatada (excepto de porcino) hasta 2 Kg', 'Miel, jalea real, polen hasta 1 Kg'. Pork: Resolución Directoral 0012-2021-MIDAGRI-SENASA-DSA prohibits pig-origin goods entering Peru (African swine fever). In-flight food (cheese, ham, etc.) may not be taken off the plane and is confiscated.
summary: Declare it. Packed, labelled dairy up to 5 kg, cured meats up to 10 kg and honey up to 1 kg are allowed; all pork is banned.

legal_source.name: ¡Amigo viajero! — Servicio Nacional de Sanidad Agraria del Perú (SENASA), gob.pe campaign page (last changed 10 May 2024)

limits.description: Declare all plant products. Up to 1 kg each of industrially dried herbs/flowers/fruit and vegetables, ground spices, edible mushrooms, flours, grains and whole spices are allowed after SENASA inspection. Fresh or naturally dried fruit and flowers, wood, live insects and plants need prior SENASA authorisation. Soil is not allowed.

notes: SENASA 'Amigo viajero': products allowed in accompanied baggage and only checked by the SENASA inspector, 'Sólo hasta 1 kg': industrially dried medicinal and aromatic herbs; industrially dried cut flowers and foliage; industrially dried fruit and vegetables; ground herbs and spices; fresh or dried edible mushrooms; flours, starches, semolina; grains; whole spices. More than that requires meeting SENASA rules before travel. 'Los productos frescos o secos naturalmente (frutas y flores), maderas, insectos vivos, plantas o partes de ellas... requieren de una autorización previa por parte del SENASA y no pueden ingresar al país en tu equipaje sin cumplir los controles fitosanitarios. No está autorizado el ingreso de suelo o tierra.' Declare plant products on the customs declaration. Queries: scv@senasa.gob.pe. SUNAT also lists 'productos agropecuarios' as restricted goods.
summary: Declare all plant products. Small amounts of dried, packaged items are allowed after inspection; fresh fruit needs SENASA authorisation.

legal_source.name: ¡Amigo viajero! — Servicio Nacional de Sanidad Agraria del Perú (SENASA), gob.pe campaign page (last changed 10 May 2024)

limits.description: Restricted: arms and ammunition need prior authorisation from the competent Peruvian authority and must be declared.

notes: SUNAT lists 'Armas y municiones' among 'Mercancía restringida que requiere autorización de una o más entidades competentes para su ingreso', which must be declared on the Declaración Jurada de Equipaje. SUNAT's page does not name the authorising body or set out the procedure; without the authorisation the item can be held in customs custody (SUNAT 'Ingresar equipaje al país'). We have not verified the authorising agency's traveller procedure.
summary: Restricted: arms and ammunition need prior authorisation from the competent Peruvian authority and must be declared.

legal_source.name: Bienes o artículos que debes declarar al entrar al Perú — SUNAT (gob.pe, last changed 14 Jan 2024)

limits.description: Recreational drones under 2 kg take-off mass fall outside Peru's RPAS regulation. Heavier drones, or any non-recreational use, must be registered with the DGAC (within 30 working days of acquisition) and non-recreational operation needs DGAC licences.

notes: D.S. N° 012-2026-MTC (Regulation of Law 30740, published 29 May 2026) applies to national and foreign persons operating RPAS. Art. 3.2(b) excludes 'La Aeronave Pilotada a Distancia de uso recreativo o aerodeportivo que tenga una masa máxima de despegue inferior a dos (2) kilogramos'. Art. 8: RPA/RPAS used in the Open or Specific category must be entered in the DGAC's Register of Remotely Piloted Aircraft (free, per NTC 001-2015) within 30 working days of acquisition. Art. 25/30: operations other than recreational use need an Open-category operating licence and a remote-pilot licence; the licence form asks for a DNI, passport or carné de extranjería. The regulation's Open/Specific-category provisions take effect only once the DGAC updates its technical rules (within two years), so NTC 001-2015 still governs in the meantime. Flights in Natural Protected Areas are supervised together with SERNANP (art. 7.2). This row covers flying rules; we found no SUNAT traveller rule specific to bringing a drone into Peru.
summary: Recreational drones under 2 kg aren't covered by Peru's drone rules; heavier ones must be registered with the DGAC.

legal_source.name: Decreto Supremo N° 012-2026-MTC — Reglamento de la Ley N° 30740 (RPAS), El Peruano, 29 May 2026

limits.description: Drinks made abroad and labelled 'pisco' may not be brought into Peru.

notes: SUNAT lists 'Bebidas fabricadas en el extranjero con la denominación “pisco”' as 'Mercancía prohibida de ingresar al territorio nacional'; prohibited goods are seized. Same list: used clothing and footwear not owned by the traveller, and used car parts.
summary: Banned: drinks made abroad and labelled "pisco" may not be brought into Peru. Prohibited goods are seized.

legal_source.name: Bienes o artículos que debes declarar al entrar al Perú — SUNAT (gob.pe, last changed 14 Jan 2024)

limits.description: Adult passengers may bring up to 5 litres of alcoholic drinks (wine, beer, rum, whisky or other liquor) free of duty.

notes: Dominican Customs (DGA) Manual del Viajero, FAQ 1: 'Los pasajeros mayores de edad pueden ingresar hasta 5 litros de bebidas alcohólicas (vino, cerveza, ron, whisky u otro licor) libres de impuestos.' The downloadable manual (PDF, Nov 2025) says the same ('Hasta cinco litros de bebida alcohólica de libre circulación'). Amounts beyond personal-baggage allowances must be declared on the E-Ticket customs section.

legal_source.name: Dirección General de Aduanas (DGA) — Manual del Viajero (traveller FAQ page)

limits.description: Duty-free: 20 packs of cigarettes, OR 25 cigars, OR 200 grams of tobacco (adult passengers).

notes: DGA Manual del Viajero, FAQ 2: 'Se permite ingresar, libre de impuestos: 20 cajetillas de cigarrillos, o 25 puros, o 200 gramos de tabaco.' The PDF manual specifies this applies to 'pasajeros mayores de edad'. The allowances are alternatives ('o'), not cumulative. E-cigarettes/vapes are not mentioned by Customs (see unverified).
summary: Duty-free for adults: 20 packs of cigarettes, or 25 cigars, or 200 g of tobacco. These are alternatives, not added together.

legal_source.name: Dirección General de Aduanas (DGA) — Manual del Viajero (traveller FAQ page)

limits.description: Cash of US$10,000 or more (or the equivalent in Dominican pesos or other currency), and bearer securities/instruments, must be declared to Customs on entry or exit using the official form, with documents showing the lawful origin of the funds. No tax is charged for carrying money.

notes: DGA Manual del Viajero: under 'Que sí necesitan declaración aduanera' — 'Dinero en efectivo US$10,000 o su equivalente en pesos dominicanos u otra moneda extranjera, títulos o valores al portador, estás obligado a declararlo ... al momento de tu entrada o salida, utilizando el formulario habilitado ... y presentar los documentos que justifiquen la procedencia lícita'. FAQ 9 says 'No se cobran impuestos por portar dinero' and phrases the trigger as 'más de US$10,000'. Wording conflict on the same page (US$10,000 vs more than US$10,000) — we show the stricter reading: declare at US$10,000 or more. The declaration is part of the E-Ticket.
summary: Declare US$10,000 or more in cash or bearer instruments, with documents showing where the money came from.

legal_source.name: Dirección General de Aduanas (DGA) — Manual del Viajero (traveller FAQ page)

limits.description: Medicines for personal use are allowed, in quantities consistent with the length of your stay and your dosage.

notes: DGA Manual del Viajero, FAQ 4: 'Los medicamentos de uso personal están permitidos.' The PDF manual: 'Los medicamentos deben ser de uso personal de conformidad con la estadía y dosis'. The same page lists 'medicinas, sujetas a regulaciones por el ... Ministerio de Salud Pública' among items needing a customs declaration, so declare medicines on the E-Ticket customs section if in doubt. Customs gives no fixed quantity.
summary: Medicines for personal use are allowed in amounts that match your stay and dosage. Customs gives no fixed quantity.

legal_source.name: Dirección General de Aduanas (DGA) — Manual del Viajero (traveller FAQ page)

limits.description: Controlled or psychotropic medicines for personal use are allowed only with the doctor's prescription that justifies their use during your stay; quantity must match your stay and dosage.

notes: DGA Manual del Viajero, FAQ 4: 'En el caso de sustancias controladas o psicotrópicas, debes presentar la receta médica que justifique su consumo durante la estadía.' PDF manual: '...debiendo mostrarse la receta médica, en caso de que se trate de sustancias psicotrópicas.' Customs does not name specific drugs. We could not find a Ministry of Public Health (DIGEMAPS) or DNCD page on travellers' controlled medication, so any extra Ministry authorisation for large quantities or particular substances is unconfirmed. Separately, Customs lists 'sustancias psicotrópicas' without a prescription among prohibited/restricted items, and Canada's advice notes the Dominican Republic's zero-tolerance policy on illegal drugs. Keep medicines in original packaging with the prescription.
summary: Allowed for personal use only with the doctor's prescription justifying its use during your stay; the amount must match your stay and dosage.

legal_source.name: Dirección General de Aduanas (DGA) — Manual del Viajero (traveller FAQ page)

items: The doctor's prescription that justifies your use of the medicine during your stay

source.name: Dirección General de Aduanas (DGA) — Manual del Viajero (traveller FAQ page)

limits.description: Covered by the general personal-medication rule: allowed for personal use in quantities consistent with your stay and dosage.

notes: Dominican Customs has no injectable-specific rule; its general rule applies: 'Los medicamentos de uso personal están permitidos' and 'deben ser de uso personal de conformidad con la estadía y dosis' (DGA Manual del Viajero, FAQ 4 and PDF manual). Insulin and GLP-1 pens (Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro) are not controlled/psychotropic substances, so the prescription requirement for psychotropics does not expressly apply — but carrying the prescription is sensible. Customs does not mention syringes, needles or cooling packs specifically. Medicines are among items 'sujetas a regulaciones por el Ministerio de Salud Pública' that the page says need a declaration.
summary: Allowed for personal use, in amounts that match your stay and dosage, under the general medicine rule. Customs has no injectable-specific rule.

legal_source.name: Dirección General de Aduanas (DGA) — Manual del Viajero (traveller FAQ page)

limits.description: No allowance. Drugs are prohibited, and the Dominican Republic has a zero-tolerance policy on illegal drugs including cannabis.

notes: DGA Manual del Viajero, FAQ 14 ('¿Qué artículos están prohibidos o restringidos?'): 'La droga, sustancias psicotrópicas, armas de fuego, sustancias contaminantes, y otras que afecten la seguridad nacional.' Canada's travel advice (travel.gc.ca/destinations/dominican-republic, updated 26 May 2026): 'The Dominican Republic has a zero-tolerance policy to illegal drugs, including cannabis. Authorities can impose severe penalties for possession of even a small quantity'; departing travellers may be drug-screened, have luggage searched or be asked to undergo an X-ray. Medical cannabis prescriptions from other countries are not recognised in any source we found. CBD: no official source addresses CBD specifically, so this row doesn't cover CBD products.
summary: Banned: drugs are prohibited, and the Dominican Republic has zero tolerance for illegal drugs, including cannabis.

legal_source.name: Dirección General de Aduanas (DGA) — Manual del Viajero (traveller FAQ page)

limits.description: All food must be declared on the customs form (E-Ticket). Animal products are subject to agricultural/animal-health rules and may be inspected or seized.

notes: DGA Manual del Viajero, FAQ 16: '¿Debo declarar productos de alimentos? Sí, se debe declarar en el formulario correspondiente' — 'ese aspecto es competencia de las autoridades de salud, sanidad vegetal, animal'. The page also lists 'productos agropecuarios, alimentos ... sujetas a regulaciones por el Ministerio de Agricultura o el Ministerio de Salud Pública' as needing declaration. We could not find an official passenger list of which meat/dairy items are banned; the animal-health authority (Dirección General de Ganadería) did not publish one we could reach. Declare and expect possible confiscation.
summary: Declare all food on the E-Ticket customs form. Animal products fall under animal-health rules and may be inspected or seized.

legal_source.name: Dirección General de Aduanas (DGA) — Manual del Viajero (traveller FAQ page)

limits.description: Plants, agricultural products and food must be declared on the customs form (E-Ticket); they are subject to Ministry of Agriculture rules and plant-quarantine inspection.

notes: DGA Manual del Viajero: 'Plantas, productos agropecuarios, alimentos y medicinas, sujetas a regulaciones por el Ministerio de Agricultura o el Ministerio de Salud Pública' are listed under items that DO need a customs declaration; FAQ 16 says foods must be declared on the form. The Ministry of Agriculture runs plant-quarantine inspection at airports, but we found no official passenger list of banned fruits/vegetables. Declare and expect possible confiscation.
summary: Declare all plants, farm products and food on the E-Ticket customs form. They face plant-quarantine inspection and may be confiscated.

legal_source.name: Dirección General de Aduanas (DGA) — Manual del Viajero (traveller FAQ page)

limits.description: Firearms are listed by Customs as prohibited or restricted items; there is no traveller allowance.

notes: DGA Manual del Viajero, FAQ 14 ('¿Qué artículos están prohibidos o restringidos?'): 'La droga, sustancias psicotrópicas, armas de fuego, sustancias contaminantes, y otras que afecten la seguridad nacional.' The page lists them as 'prohibidos o restringidos' and does not describe any permit route for tourists; we did not research whether a separate firearm import authorisation exists (e.g. for sport shooting). Do not bring firearms or ammunition without prior written authorisation from the Dominican authorities. Knives, pepper spray and replica weapons are not mentioned.
summary: Firearms are on Customs' prohibited or restricted list, with no traveller allowance. Don't bring them without prior written authorisation.

legal_source.name: Dirección General de Aduanas (DGA) — Manual del Viajero (traveller FAQ page)

limits.description: Flying a drone is regulated by IDAC under RAD 107: the operator and the drone must be registered, prior permits are needed for flights in urban areas or near crowds, restricted zones and height limits apply, and you must keep visual line of sight.

notes: IDAC (Instituto Dominicano de Aviación Civil) notice 'Idac advierte sobre uso de drones sin autorización en el Centro Olímpico Juan Pablo Duarte' (2026): 'el Rad 107 establece obligaciones como el registro del operador y del dron, la solicitud previa de permisos para vuelos en áreas urbanas o cercanas a multitudes, el respeto a zonas restringidas y límites de altura, así como la obligación de mantener contacto visual con la aeronave en todo momento.' A separate 2026 IDAC notice banned unauthorised drone flights near all venues of the XXV Central American and Caribbean Games (Santo Domingo, Boca Chica, Baní, San Cristóbal, Bonao, Santiago, Puerto Plata, Punta Cana); misuse can bring administrative sanctions. An older IDAC notice (2024) lists airports, the National Palace, the Ministry of Defence, San Isidro Air Base, the oil refinery, Las Calderas naval base and military camps as restricted zones. Customs does not mention drones; the duty-free electronics allowance lists one camera, two phones, one laptop and one tablet, so a drone could be assessed for duty. No source states a weight threshold under RAD 107 (an older IDAC notice mentioned permits for drones over 4.4 lb under the former RAD-48).
summary: The drone and operator must be registered with IDAC; urban flights need permits.

legal_source.name: IDAC — Idac advierte sobre uso de drones sin autorización en el Centro Olímpico Juan Pablo Duarte (RAD 107)

limits.description: Personal effects are duty-free. Electronics duty-free per traveller: 1 photo/video camera, 2 mobile phones, 1 laptop and 1 tablet, sound devices, 1 musical instrument. Gifts up to US$500 total, usable once every 3 months.

notes: DGA Manual del Viajero (FAQ 8, 11, 13) and PDF manual: '1 laptop y 1 tablet (nuevas o usadas). Si llevas una segunda laptop o más, deberás pagar los impuestos'; 'Una cámara fotográfica y de video por viajero. Dos teléfonos celulares'; gifts 'por un valor total de hasta USD$500.00 ... solo puede ser utilizada y aplicada una vez cada (3) meses' (PDF: 2–3 units per gift type, not repeated). Children: a stroller, car seat, playpen and 5 toys each. Personal sports equipment in reasonable, non-commercial quantities is duty-free.

legal_source.name: Dirección General de Aduanas (DGA) — Manual del Viajero (traveller FAQ page)

limits.description: Counts toward the general USD 2,000 duty-free baggage allowance; no more than 10 units of the same kind (more is treated as a commercial shipment). Excess value pays a 15% single tax.
limits.quantity: Within USD 2,000 total; max 10 units of same kind

notes: Decreto 1165 de 2019: Art. 268 – travellers may bring accompanied baggage 'hasta por un valor total de dos mil dólares ... (USD 2.000)' free of the tributo único (minors get a reduced share, Art. 274); Art. 266 – up to 'diez (10) unidades de la misma clase, por viajero' of goods for personal/family use or gifts is not a commercial shipment; Art. 270 – excess pays a 15% ad valorem single tax. No separate litre/carton quota for this product appears in the customs decree: it simply counts toward the general duty-free allowance. Goods above the allowance must be declared on DIAN Form 530; undeclared goods subject to the tax can be seized (Art. 267 par. 2). Separately, gov.uk notes drinking alcohol in public spaces is illegal.

legal_source.name: Decreto 1165 de 2019 (Régimen de Aduanas), Arts. 266–270 – DIAN normograma

limits.description: Counts toward the general USD 2,000 duty-free baggage allowance; no more than 10 units of the same kind per traveller. Excess value pays a 15% single tax.
limits.quantity: Within USD 2,000 total; max 10 units of same kind

notes: Same legal basis as alcohol: Decreto 1165 de 2019 Arts. 266 (10 units of the same class = not commercial), 268 (USD 2,000 franchise) and 270 (15% single tax on the excess). No separate litre/carton quota for this product appears in the customs decree: it simply counts toward the general duty-free allowance. What counts as one 'unit' (pack vs carton) is not defined in the decree — keep quantities clearly personal. Declare anything over the allowance on DIAN Form 530.

legal_source.name: Decreto 1165 de 2019 (Régimen de Aduanas), Arts. 266–270 – DIAN normograma

limits.description: Declare cash, Colombian pesos or monetary instruments over USD 10,000 (or equivalent) on DIAN Form 530, both entering and leaving.

notes: DIAN: travellers must file the 'Declaración de Equipaje, de Dinero o Títulos representativos de Dinero – Viajeros' (Form 530) when the amount in foreign currency, Colombian cash or monetary instruments exceeds 'USD 10.000 ... o su equivalente en otras monedas'; amounts up to USD 10,000 need no declaration. DIAN's Form 530 page states the same threshold. Cross-checked: gov.uk ('You can bring up to 10,000 US dollars-worth of any currency ... declare anything above this amount with ... DIAN'). Undeclared excess may be retained by customs (per DIAN Form 530 page; exact sanction not re-read).

legal_source.name: Trámites aduaneros – Viajeros – DIAN

limits.description: USD 2,000 of goods duty-free per adult (personal effects not counted); above that, up to USD 3,000 more with a 15% single tax if you were abroad at least 5 days (once a year).

notes: Decreto 1165 de 2019 Art. 268: duty-free accompanied baggage up to USD 2,000; personal effects are not counted. Art. 269: travellers abroad at least 5 calendar days may bring, paying the 15% single tax (Art. 270), up to 3 units each of household, sports and professional articles and up to 10 units of the same kind of other personal goods, up to USD 3,000 total, once per year per person. Art. 274: minors get a reduced quota (DIAN page: 50%). Art. 276: non-residents may temporarily import, tax-free and subject to re-export, items needed for personal or professional use during their stay if declared on arrival. DIAN's 'Trámites aduaneros' page repeats the USD 2,000 franchise and 15% tax. Note: the English version of DIAN's Form 530 page mentions a 'USD 5,000' quota that the Spanish page and the decree do not — the decree controls.
summary: USD 2,000 of goods duty-free per adult; up to USD 3,000 more at a 15% single tax, once a year.

legal_source.name: Decreto 1165 de 2019 (Régimen de Aduanas), Arts. 266–270 – DIAN normograma

limits.description: No Colombian traveller allowance found. Carry personal quantities in original containers with a copy of your prescription; check legality yourself.

notes: No primary Colombian rule specific to travellers' personal medication was found (DIAN, INVIMA and the Fondo Nacional de Estupefacientes pages searched). Customs law treats 'efectos personales' — new or used articles a traveller may need for personal use during the trip — as outside the duty-free quota (Decreto 1165 de 2019, Art. 3 definition, as modified by Decreto 360 de 2021), but does not mention medicines. The UK government's Colombia travel advice says: 'If you take prescription medication, you will be responsible for determining its legality in Colombia. Always keep your medication in the original container, bring sufficient quantities ..., pack your medication in your carry-on luggage and carry a copy of your prescriptions', and that Colombian prescriptions 'must be written in Spanish, in the metric system and using the medicine's generic name'. travel.gc.ca adds that some prescription medicines are unavailable in Colombia and adrenaline auto-injectors are not sold there.

legal_source.name: Colombia travel advice – Health (updated 2026-10-06) – GOV.UK / FCDO

limits.description: Bringing cannabis into Colombia without a licence is a crime, even in transit and even in small amounts.

notes: Código Penal (Ley 599 de 2000) Art. 376 as modified by Ley 1453 de 2011: anyone who 'sin permiso de autoridad competente, introduzca al país, así sea en tránsito o saque de él' narcotic or psychotropic substances faces 128–360 months' prison; if the quantity does not exceed 1,000 g of marijuana or 200 g of hashish the penalty is 64–108 months. The only carve-out (added by Ley 1787 de 2016) is medical/scientific cannabis use under licences from the Ministry of Health or Ministry of Justice. Domestic 'personal dose' rules do not authorise import. CBD products are not specifically addressed by this source — treat as unverified. Travel advice (gov.uk) also stresses severe penalties for drug possession and trafficking.
summary: Banned: bringing cannabis into Colombia without a licence is a crime, even in transit and in small amounts.

legal_source.name: Ley 599 de 2000 (Código Penal), Art. 376 – Secretaría del Senado

transit.description: Colombia's criminal code makes bringing cannabis into the country without a licence a crime "even in transit" (así sea en tránsito).

source.name: Ley 599 de 2000 (Código Penal), Art. 376 – Secretaría del Senado

limits.description: Sealed, commercially labelled cured/cooked meats, boneless aged hams and aged/processed cheeses up to 6 kg each; processed honey and pre-cooked shrimp up to 3 kg. Pork products from Spain and Germany currently banned.

notes: ICA (12 Apr 2017 notice, under Resolución ICA 3865 de 2005): animal-origin food may enter without an import document only in its original sealed packaging labelled with country, establishment, packing and expiry dates: cooked or cured hermetically packed sausages/meat products up to 6 kg; boneless hams up to 6 kg each (Spanish serrano aged >190 days, ibérico >365 days, Italian >400 days, others >180 days); aged, processed or spreadable sealed cheeses up to 6 kg; processed/pasteurised honey up to 3 kg; pre-cooked sealed shrimp up to 3 kg. Excluded: bovine meat products from BSE countries; cured pork from Italy and from countries with African or classical swine fever. Current restriction: ICA Resolución 00031675 (4 Dec 2025) Art. 3 prohibits pork products from Spain carried as accompanied baggage 'independientemente de la cantidad' (unless meeting OMSA Code art. 15.1.2), and Resolución 00034883 (30 Dec 2025) does the same for Germany, both until lifted. Non-compliant goods are held for re-shipment within 5 days or seized and incinerated. Declare animal products on the DIAN baggage declaration. Caveat: the quantity list comes from a 2017 ICA notice; no newer consolidated traveller list was found.

legal_source.name: El ICA hace recomendaciones a viajeros internacionales sobre el ingreso al país de productos de origen vegetal y animal (12 Apr 2017) – Instituto Colombiano Agropecuario (ICA)

limits.description: Plants, seeds, propagation material and fresh fruit/vegetables need a phytosanitary certificate from the origin country; otherwise they may be seized.

notes: ICA (12 Apr 2017 notice): products must arrive with 'el correspondiente certificado zoosanitario o fitosanitario' from the country of origin; plants of all species, planting/propagation material and fresh fruits and vegetables that don't comply may be seized because they can carry pests. Non-compliant goods are held for re-shipment within 5 days or seized and incinerated. Travellers must declare plants and plant products on the baggage declaration (DIAN lists 'vegetales, animales y productos reglamentados' among cases requiring Form 530). Caveat: 2017 notice; no newer traveller page found.

legal_source.name: El ICA hace recomendaciones a viajeros internacionales sobre el ingreso al país de productos de origen vegetal y animal (12 Apr 2017) – Instituto Colombiano Agropecuario (ICA)

limits.description: Importing firearms into Colombia is illegal.

notes: Government of Canada travel advice for Colombia (updated 2026-10-06): 'It's illegal to import firearms into Colombia.' Other weapons (knives, pepper spray, etc.) are not covered by this source. The underlying Colombian statute (Decreto 2535 de 1993 on arms) was not read in this pass.

legal_source.name: Travel advice and advisories for Colombia (updated 2026-10-06) – Government of Canada

limits.description: Drones may only be brought in through El Dorado International Airport (Bogotá), with a customs form on arrival stating the drone's use.

notes: Government of Canada travel advice for Colombia (updated 2026-10-06): 'You may only bring drones into Colombia through El Dorado International Airport in Bogotá' and you must complete a customs form on arrival confirming the drone's intended use. Flying rules (Aerocivil RAC 100 registration/operation requirements) were not verified in this pass.

legal_source.name: Travel advice and advisories for Colombia (updated 2026-10-06) – Government of Canada

limits.description: Clothes and personal items, one phone and one notebook/tablet are duty-free. Other goods bought abroad: USD 500 by air or sea (plus USD 500 at the arrival duty-free shop); USD 300 by land or river (no arrival duty-free allowance, except USD 500 at Puerto Iguazú). Under-16s get 50%. Monthly, not cumulative. Above the allowance you pay 50% of the excess and must declare.

notes: ARCA (customs) pages 'Franquicias', 'Objetos permitidos' and 'Régimen de equipaje' (read 2026-10-09). Families (spouses, partners, children under 16) may pool allowances. Goods for commercial purposes are prohibited under the baggage regime. You only have to declare if you exceed the allowance, carry SENASA-regulated goods, or carry USD 10,000+ in cash; use the digital baggage declaration (mobile app / self-service kiosks) or form OM-2087/G5 or G6. ARCA gives no separate litre/stick limits for alcohol or tobacco on these pages — see unverified rows.

legal_source.name: ARCA (Aduana) — ¿Cuál es la franquicia de ingreso?

limits.description: Entering with cash or monetary instruments (foreign or Argentine currency) worth USD 10,000 or more must be declared to customs on form OM 2249A. For under-16s the limit is USD 5,000. Amounts above USD 10,000 can only leave Argentina by bank transfer.

notes: ARCA 'Ingreso y egreso de valores': amounts under USD 10,000 may be brought in freely; higher amounts need a special declaration (OM 2249A). ARCA 'Régimen de equipaje' says to declare when 'igual o superior al equivalente a USD 10.000'. Conversion uses the Banco de la Nación buying rate at close of the previous business day. Cross-check: gov.uk Argentina advice says declare cash/travellers cheques over USD 10,000; Spain MFA says the same applies on entry and exit.
summary: Declare cash worth US$10,000 or more (US$5,000 for under-16s) on form OM 2249A when you arrive.

legal_source.name: ARCA (Aduana) — ¿Qué importes pueden ingresarse y/o retirarse del país?

limits.description: Carry a legalised medical prescription. Under the Mercosur rule applied in Argentina, it must show your name and address; the medicine, active ingredient, strength, form, quantity and dosage; and the date, name, address, signature and registration of the prescriber. It must be authorised by the health authority. Patients in transit present this document to health or police authorities at the airport or border.

notes: Source: argentina.gob.ar Derecho Fácil summary of Mercosur GMC Resolution 66/2000, which ANMAT applies. It covers travel between Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay and Venezuela, and no official page was found on how travellers from outside Mercosur are treated, so confirm with ANMAT before travelling. ARCA lists 'Estupefacientes' as prohibited in baggage. ANMAT's control lists include methadone, hydrocodone and hydromorphone (narcotics, Ley 17.818) and amphetamine, alprazolam, clonazepam, diazepam and lorazepam (psychotropics, Ley 19.303). Methylphenidate was not checked. Medicines not registered in Argentina may need an ANMAT exceptional-access (RAEM-NR) authorisation; that procedure is for imports and may not cover a traveller's own supply.
summary: Carry a legalised prescription that meets the Mercosur rule and is authorised by the health authority.

legal_source.name: Argentina.gob.ar Derecho Fácil — Mercosur: Traslado de medicamentos (Resolución GMC 66/2000)

transit.description: If you're in transit through Argentina with medicine containing narcotic or psychotropic substances, carry a legal document with your name and address, the medicine, its active ingredient, strength, form, quantity and dosage, and your doctor's name, address, registration and signature. Show it to the health or police authorities at the airport or border.

source.name: Argentina.gob.ar Derecho Fácil — Mercosur: Traslado de medicamentos (Resolución GMC 66/2000)

limits.description: Do not bring cannabis. Customs prohibits narcotics ('Estupefacientes') in baggage, and ANMAT lists cannabis, its resin, and cannabis extracts and tinctures as Lista I narcotics under Ley 17.818.

notes: Sources: the ARCA 'Objetos permitidos y prohibiciones' page, plus the ANMAT controlled-substances list (argentina.gob.ar/sites/default/files/estupefacientes_2016.pdf, linked from the ANMAT 'Listados' page): 'CANNABIS (Marihuana), su resina (Haschisch) y los extractos y tinturas de Cannabis — LISTA I. LEY 17818/68'. No official page read deals with CBD-only products for travellers. The list's 'extractos y tinturas de Cannabis' covers oils extracted from cannabis, which is how most CBD oils are made; for a CBD product made another way, ask ANMAT. Argentina's medical-cannabis programme is for registered patients in Argentina and does not give foreign travellers an allowance.
summary: Banned: cannabis and its extracts are Lista I narcotics, and customs prohibits narcotics in baggage.

legal_source.name: ARCA (Aduana) — ¿Qué objetos se pueden ingresar? (Prohibiciones: Estupefacientes); ANMAT Listado de Sustancias Controladas — Estupefacientes

limits.description: Prohibited: meat of any species, cured/processed meats, sausages, hams, honey and other bee products, homemade food, and any food without a label. Exceptions: canned fish, pork or poultry. Boneless Spanish serrano/ibérico ham, sliced or in pieces, is allowed if it is factory vacuum-packed and labelled. Allowed items must be packaged, labelled and in personal quantities.

notes: SENASA page 'Ingresar o regresar al país con alimentos' (Resolution 295/1999). The Spanish-ham exception comes from Res. 655/2017. Ibérico loin (lomo) from Spain has been suspended (Res. 940/2025). SENASA may confiscate products without the required authorisation. ARCA says SENASA-regulated goods must be declared.

legal_source.name: SENASA — Ingresar o regresar al país con alimentos

limits.description: Allowed in personal quantities if packaged and labelled by the producer under official health control: pasteurised milk, condensed milk, milk powder, yogurt, butter, dulce de leche, and cheeses made from pasteurised milk. Other dairy products and derivatives are on the 'not permitted' list.

notes: SENASA 'Ingresar o regresar al país con alimentos' (Res. 295/1999). The page lists 'productos y derivados lácteos' as not permitted, apart from the authorised items above. Treat raw-milk cheese and unlabelled dairy as prohibited. Declare SENASA-regulated goods on arrival.
summary: Packaged, labelled pasteurised dairy such as milk powder, yogurt, butter, dulce de leche and cheese is allowed.

legal_source.name: SENASA — Ingresar o regresar al país con alimentos

limits.description: Prohibited: fresh fruit and vegetables; flowers and garden plants; fruit, ornamental and forestry plants; plant parts such as seeds, roots and buds. Allowed in personal quantities if packaged and labelled: processed fruit and vegetables (in syrup, pickled, canned), roasted or salted nuts, jams, candied fruit, juices, sugar and oil.

notes: SENASA 'Ingresar o regresar al país con alimentos' (Res. 295/1999). Also prohibited: animal feed, veterinary products, insects and microorganisms. A separate SENASA barrier also restricts some fruit and meat entering Patagonia from the rest of Argentina.
summary: Fresh fruit, vegetables, plants and seeds are banned. Packaged processed fruit, nuts and jams are allowed.

legal_source.name: SENASA — Ingresar o regresar al país con alimentos

limits.description: Firearms and explosives are prohibited in baggage unless the national firearms authority (RENAR, formerly ANMAC) has authorised them in advance. Flammables are also excluded.

notes: The ARCA 'Objetos permitidos y prohibiciones' page reads 'Armas, explosivos (salvo autorización del RENAR)'. ARCA's 2018 baggage infographic names the authority as ANMAC. Contact the firearms authority well before travel, for example for hunting trips. No authorisation procedure was read.
summary: Firearms and explosives are banned in baggage without prior authorisation from the national firearms authority.

legal_source.name: ARCA (Aduana) — ¿Qué objetos se pueden ingresar?

limits.description: Up to 1 litre of alcohol duty-free per traveller; more than 1 litre is subject to customs duty.

notes: German Foreign Office (Stand 09.10.2026): 'Bis zu 1 l Alkohol ... dürfen zollfrei mitgeführt werden.' Cross-checked with Japan MOFA (updated 22 Apr 2026): bringing more than 1 litre of alcohol into Jordan incurs duty; if you enter overland with more than 1 litre and plan to take it out later by air, you pay a cash deposit (JOD only) at the border, refunded when customs checks the alcohol on departure. Jordan Customs' own site (customs.gov.jo) was IP-blocked from our environment, so the controlling customs text was not read. Public drinking is banned outside some hotels and restaurants (France Diplomatie).

legal_source.name: Auswärtiges Amt — Jordanien: Reise- und Sicherheitshinweise (Einreise und Zoll)

limits.description: 200 cigarettes and 200 g of tobacco duty-free per traveller.

notes: German Foreign Office (Stand 09.10.2026): 'außerdem 200 Zigaretten und 200 g Tabak dürfen zollfrei mitgeführt werden.' The 200-cigarette figure also appears in Jordan's AIP GEN 1.3 (Civil Aviation Regulatory Commission, dated 01 Nov 2006 — old). Jordan Customs' own site was IP-blocked. Rules for cigars as a separate allowance were not confirmed.

limits.description: Import of weapons is prohibited.

notes: German Foreign Office: 'Die Einfuhr von Waffen, Drohnen, Funkgeräten, Rauschgift und pornografischen Schriften ist verboten.' Japan MOFA (22 Apr 2026): narcotics, firearms and pornography may not be brought in. Knives specifically are not addressed by either source; the verdict covers weapons/firearms generally.

limits.description: Only with prior approval from Jordan's Civil Aviation Regulatory Commission; without a permit the drone is held/confiscated at the border.

notes: UK FCDO: 'You must apply for approval to take a drone into Jordan at least 10 working days before you travel. If you have not received a permit before you arrive, the authorities will hold your drone at the airport. You can collect it when you leave Jordan.' Canada: 'You must obtain authorization before importing or operating a drone'; violations can mean imprisonment, fines or confiscation. CONFLICT: France Diplomatie says drones 'sont interdits à l'arrivée en Jordanie et sont systématiquement confisqués', and Germany lists drones among prohibited imports. The CARC publishes a 'Drones Operations Approval Application Form' (https://carc.gov.jo/en/drones). Treat a drone as not importable unless you hold CARC approval before you travel.

legal_source.name: GOV.UK (FCDO) — Jordan travel advice: Entry requirements (Customs rules, Drones)

procedure.title: Get drone approval from Jordan's Civil Aviation Regulatory Commission
