steps: Fill in CARC's Drones Operations Approval Application Form, published on its drones page.
Apply at least 10 working days before you travel.
Travel with the permit. Without one, the authorities hold your drone at the airport, and you collect it when you leave Jordan.
procedure.atTheBorder: If you haven't received a permit before you arrive, your drone is held at the airport until you leave.

limits.description: Narcotics, including cannabis, may not be imported; drug offences are punished severely even for tiny amounts.

notes: German Foreign Office: import of 'Rauschgift' is prohibited, and drug offences are punished 'schon bei geringsten Mengen und bei jeder Art von Drogen mit langjährigen Haftstrafen (bis lebenslänglich)'. Japan MOFA: narcotics may not be brought in and their import, possession and use are severely punished. France: drug possession/use/trade severely punished, with prison plus permanent ban from the territory. CBD products are not specifically addressed by any source read — do not assume CBD is allowed.
summary: Banned: narcotics, including cannabis, may not be imported into Jordan; drug offences are punished severely even for tiny amounts.

legal_source.name: Auswärtiges Amt — Jordanien: Reise- und Sicherheitshinweise (Einreise und Zoll)

limits.description: Pornographic material may not be imported — Japan notes even weekly magazines with semi-nude photos can be refused.

notes: Japan MOFA (22 Apr 2026): pornography may not be brought in, including magazines carrying semi-nude photos. Germany also lists 'pornografische Schriften' as prohibited imports.

legal_source.name: 外務省 海外安全ホームページ — ヨルダン 安全対策基礎データ（通関・外貨申告）

limits.description: Import of radio transceivers (Funkgeräte) is prohibited.

notes: German Foreign Office lists 'Funkgeräte' (radio devices) among prohibited imports. Single source; no Jordanian telecom-regulator page was read, so licensed exceptions are unknown.

legal_source.name: Auswärtiges Amt — Jordanien: Reise- und Sicherheitshinweise (Einreise und Zoll)

limits.description: Travel items including a laptop and camera may be brought in duty-free but must be taken out again.

notes: German Foreign Office: 'Reisebedarf inklusive Laptop und Kamera darf zollfrei eingeführt werden, muss aber wieder ausgeführt werden.' Separately, Jordan strictly bans exporting antiquities without Department of Antiquities authorisation (France Diplomatie, Law 21/1998) and Germany also mentions corals.

legal_source.name: Auswärtiges Amt — Jordanien: Reise- und Sicherheitshinweise (Einreise und Zoll)

limits.description: 5 litres of wine, aguardiente or liquor per adult traveller, duty-free, as part of baggage

notes: Art. 365(j) of the customs regulation (Decreto 44051-H) counts as duty-free traveller baggage 'Quinientos gramos de tabaco elaborado, cinco litros de vino, aguardiente o licor, por cada viajero mayor de edad y hasta dos kilogramos de golosinas.' The text does not mention beer separately; it says 'wine, aguardiente or liquor'. Baggage must be for personal use, not commercial. Anything above the allowance counts as goods other than baggage (see the US$500-equivalent allowance row) and must be declared on the Declaración de Viajero (art. 368).

legal_source.name: Reglamento a la Ley General de Aduanas, Decreto Ejecutivo N° 44051-H (18 May 2023), arts. 365–371 — SCIJ/Sinalevi, Procuraduría General de la República

limits.description: 500 g of manufactured tobacco per adult traveller, duty-free, as part of baggage

notes: Art. 365(j) Decreto 44051-H: 'Quinientos gramos de tabaco elaborado … por cada viajero mayor de edad'. The regulation states the allowance by weight, not by number of cigarettes. Amounts above it must be declared and taxes paid. E-cigarettes are not covered by this row (see unverified).

legal_source.name: Reglamento a la Ley General de Aduanas, Decreto Ejecutivo N° 44051-H (18 May 2023), arts. 365–371 — SCIJ/Sinalevi, Procuraduría General de la República

limits.description: Declare cash and/or títulos valores (securities/bearer instruments) of US$10,000 or more (or the equivalent in other currency) when entering or leaving

notes: Art. 35 Ley 8204 as quoted in Decreto 44096: 'Al ingresar en el país o salir de él, toda persona, nacional o extranjera, estará obligada a declarar el dinero efectivo o los títulos valores que porte, si la cantidad es igual o superior a los diez mil dólares … (US$10.000,00) o su equivalente en otra moneda.' The 'Declaración de dinero en efectivo y/o títulos valores' form (issued by the Instituto Costarricense sobre Drogas) is available at the migration posts; it must be completed and signed before finishing immigration and handed to Customs (arts. 4, 8, 11, 17). Failing to declare, or declaring a different amount, means 'la pérdida inmediata del dinero en efectivo y/o títulos valores a favor del Instituto Costarricense sobre Drogas' (art. 5) — it does not stop you entering or leaving. The threshold is 'igual o superior' — exactly US$10,000 must be declared. Cross-check: GOV.UK also says declare cash/travellers cheques of US$10,000 or more.

legal_source.name: Decreto Ejecutivo N° 44096-MP-H-MAG-MOPT-MGP-MSP, Reglamento al artículo 35 de la Ley N° 8204 (cash and bearer-instrument declarations) — SCIJ/Sinalevi, Procuraduría General de la República

limits.description: Medicines for your own use, in quantities consistent with your circumstances and needs, enter duty-free as baggage; controlled (narcotic/psychotropic) medicines have extra rules

notes: Art. 365(c) Decreto 44051-H includes in traveller baggage 'Medicamentos, alimentos, instrumentos, aparatos médicos, higiénicos o de tocador y artículos desechables utilizados con estos, en cantidades acordes con las circunstancias y necesidades del viajero.' Baggage must not be commercial. If your medicine contains a narcotic or psychotropic substance, see controlled-medication-cr: more than one month's supply needs Ministry of Health authorisation. Cross-check: travel.gc.ca advises keeping medicines in the original container, in carry-on, with paper and electronic copies of prescriptions.

legal_source.name: Reglamento a la Ley General de Aduanas, Decreto Ejecutivo N° 44051-H (18 May 2023), arts. 365–371 — SCIJ/Sinalevi, Procuraduría General de la República

limits.description: Up to one month of treatment: no authorisation needed. More than one month: Ministry of Health authorisation, applied for at least one month before travel. Never allowed: 1961 Convention List IV narcotics and fentanyl in ampoules

notes: Art. 57 Decreto 45161-S (2025): 'El Ministerio de Salud autorizará a los viajeros el ingreso o salida de preparados farmacéuticos que contienen estupefacientes o psicotrópicos cuando la cantidad supere un mes de tratamiento' — apply at least one month before travel with: ID copy (for digital filing), copies of the prescription and epicrisis and/or medical report issued no more than 3 months earlier stating diagnosis and prescribed medicines, and a copy of the purchase invoice if bought abroad. 'Si las cantidades son menores a un mes de tratamiento, esta autorización no es requerida. Los viajeros internacionales no pueden llevar consigo los estupefacientes incluidos en la Lista IV de la Convención Única de 1961 de Estupefacientes, ni fentanilo en ampollas aun cuando se permita su uso en el país de origen.' Which substances are controlled: the Ministry of Health 'Lista de sustancias sometidas a fiscalización nacional' (SCIJ, dated 11 Sep 2026; https://sinalevi.go.cr/ResultadosNormativa/Informacion?param1=107827&param2=152346&param3=1) lists, among others, METILFENIDATO, ANFETAMINA, DEXANFETAMINA, ALPRAZOLAM, CLONAZEPAM, DIAZEPAM, LORAZEPAM, ZOLPIDEM, OXICODONA, CODEINA, MORFINA and FENTANILO. Brand names in the search terms are mapped to those ingredients for search only (Adderall = amphetamine salts; Ritalin = methylphenidate; Xanax = alprazolam; Valium = diazepam); the sources name ingredients, not brands. Lisdexamfetamine (Vyvanse) and tramadol were not found as entries in the list text read, so they are deliberately not named here.

legal_source.name: Decreto Ejecutivo N° 45161-S, Reglamento para el control de drogas, estupefacientes y psicotrópicas (17 Jun 2025), art. 57 — SCIJ/Sinalevi, Procuraduría General de la República

procedure.title: For more than one month's supply: get Ministry of Health authorisation
procedure.authority: Ministry of Health (Ministerio de Salud), Costa Rica
procedure.leadTime: At least one month before you travel
documents: A copy of your ID (for digital filing).
Copies of your prescription and your epicrisis and/or medical report, issued no more than 3 months earlier, stating the diagnosis and the prescribed medicines.
A copy of the purchase invoice, if you bought the medicine abroad.
steps: Up to one month of treatment, no authorisation is needed.
For more than one month, apply to the Ministry of Health at least one month before you travel.
Include your ID copy, your prescription, your epicrisis or medical report (no more than 3 months old) and, if you bought the medicine abroad, the purchase invoice.

sources.name: Decreto Ejecutivo N° 45161-S, Reglamento para el control de drogas, estupefacientes y psicotrópicas (17 Jun 2025), art. 57 — SCIJ/Sinalevi, Procuraduría General de la República

limits.description: Medicines plus the medical instruments and disposable items used with them (syringes, pen needles) enter duty-free as baggage in quantities matching your needs

notes: Art. 365(c) Decreto 44051-H covers 'Medicamentos … instrumentos, aparatos médicos … y artículos desechables utilizados con estos, en cantidades acordes con las circunstancias y necesidades del viajero' — this is a general rule; it does not name insulin or GLP-1 brands. Insulin, semaglutide (Ozempic/Wegovy) and tirzepatide (Mounjaro) are not narcotics/psychotropics, so the one-month controlled-medicine authorisation (Decreto 45161-S art. 57) does not apply to them as such. Keep the prescription with you; airline rules on carrying needles and cooling packs are separate from customs.

legal_source.name: Reglamento a la Ley General de Aduanas, Decreto Ejecutivo N° 44051-H (18 May 2023), arts. 365–371 — SCIJ/Sinalevi, Procuraduría General de la República

limits.description: Tourists may bring hunting shotguns/rifles (up to four different hunting/target guns) and 500 rounds as baggage, but only subject to the Ley de Armas y Explosivos permit rules

notes: Art. 365(k) Decreto 44051-H: 'Escopeta o rifles de caza y quinientos tiros, incluso hasta cuatro armas diferentes para cacería o para tiro al blanco … siempre que se demuestre, en forma fehaciente, que el viajero es turista. El ingreso de armas y municiones estará sujeto a las regulaciones que sobre esta materia establece la Ley de Armas y Explosivos.' The customs rule only makes them duty-free baggage; the permit requirements under the Arms and Explosives Law were not verified here — do not travel with a firearm without confirming them with the Costa Rican authorities first. Handguns and other weapons are not covered by the baggage allowance.
summary: Tourists may bring up to four hunting guns and 500 rounds, subject to permits under Costa Rica's firearms law.

legal_source.name: Reglamento a la Ley General de Aduanas, Decreto Ejecutivo N° 44051-H (18 May 2023), arts. 365–371 — SCIJ/Sinalevi, Procuraduría General de la República

limits.description: Goods that are not baggage are tax-free up to 500 Central American pesos in total customs value, once every 6 months, if you were out of Costa Rica at least 72 hours

notes: Art. 115 Ley 7557: 'Las mercancías que la persona traiga consigo, que no constituyan equipaje, no estarán sujetas al pago de tributos hasta por un monto de quinientos pesos centroamericanos … Para estos efectos, la persona deberá permanecer un mínimo de setenta y dos horas fuera del país y no tendrá derecho a disfrutar, de nuevo, de este beneficio hasta que hayan transcurrido los seis meses siguientes a su arribo.' Reglamento 44051-H arts. 370–371: proved with your passport; not cumulative, personal, not for commercial quantities or prohibited goods. The Central American peso is a regional unit of account; the texts read do not give a dollar figure. Above the limit, customs prepares the declaration and you pay the taxes (art. 366). Normal personal baggage (clothes, one laptop, one phone, one camera, sports gear, etc., art. 365) is duty-free on top of this.

legal_source.name: Ley General de Aduanas N° 7557, arts. 114–115 (current consolidated version 11 of 11), Sistema Costarricense de Información Jurídica (SCIJ/Sinalevi), Procuraduría General de la República

notes: Travellers may not bring alcohol into Qatar. Auswärtiges Amt (Stand 09.10.2026): 'Die Einfuhr von Drogen, Alkohol, pornografischen Materials sowie religiöser Bücher und Materialien ist strengstens untersagt.' Cross-checked: Japan MOFA lists 酒類（みりん等の調味料を含む） — alcoholic drinks, including cooking seasonings such as mirin — among prohibited imports; Nederland Wereldwijd: 'Neem geen alcohol en varkensvlees(producten) mee naar Qatar'; France Diplomatie also lists alcohol as prohibited. Inside Qatar alcohol is sold only in licensed hotels/restaurants/bars and to resident permit holders (GOV.UK); public drinking can mean up to 6 months' prison or a QAR 3,000 fine. Note: alcohol is not on the customs.gov.qa tariff prohibited-goods list, and no Qatari-authority page stating the import ban was read; the verdict rests on three travellers' governments that agree.

legal_source.name: Auswärtiges Amt — Katar: Reise- und Sicherheitshinweise, 'Einreise und Zoll' (Stand 09.10.2026)

limits.description: Declare cash (Qatari riyals or foreign currency), bearer instruments (travellers cheques, cheques, money orders, promissory notes), precious metals (gold, silver, platinum) or precious stones worth more than QAR 50,000 in total, on the customs declaration form, when entering or leaving Qatar.

notes: GOV.UK: 'If you are taking money, precious metals or gems worth more than 50,000 Qatari riyals into Qatar, you must complete a declaration form', covering currency, travellers cheques, money orders, cheques, promissory notes, precious metals and precious stones; breaking the rules can mean fines, imprisonment or seizure. Cross-checked: Auswärtiges Amt says import or export above QAR 50,000 must be declared on the General Authority of Customs form on entry and exit, and violations are punished by imprisonment, fine or seizure; Government of Canada says the same for 'more than QAR50,000' when entering or leaving. Carrying it is legal; failing to declare is the offence.
summary: Declare cash, bearer instruments, precious metals or stones worth more than QAR 50,000 in total.

legal_source.name: GOV.UK (FCDO) — Qatar travel advice: Entry requirements (updated 19 Aug 2026)

limits.description: Carry a prescription and a medical report in English or Arabic, issued within the last 6 months, with details of your medication and treatment. Some prescription and over-the-counter medicines are controlled in Qatar and need a Ministry of Public Health permit (see controlled-medication-qa).

notes: GOV.UK (Health page, updated 19 Aug 2026): 'Some prescribed and over-the-counter medicines may be controlled substances in Qatar. If you need to bring controlled or prescription medication into Qatar, make sure you follow the steps required by the Qatar Ministry of Public Health, including carrying a prescription and medical report in English or Arabic containing details of your medication and treatment, issued within the last 6 months.' Auswärtiges Amt lists what the report should contain: patient details, diagnosis, treatment plan and duration, dosage recommendations, scientific and brand name, dose and quantity, a legible stamp of the doctor/clinic, on the clinic's letterhead, plus a copy of your passport. Nederland Wereldwijd: keep medicines in the original packaging. Check whether your medicine is on Qatar's controlled lists before travelling.
summary: Carry a prescription and a medical report under 6 months old. Some medicines need a Ministry of Public Health permit.

legal_source.name: GOV.UK (FCDO) — Qatar travel advice: Entry requirements (updated 19 Aug 2026)

limits.description: Narcotic and psychoactive medicines: up to 30 days' supply or the length of your stay, whichever is shorter. Psychotropic medicines: up to 2 months' supply. Needs a Ministry of Public Health permit, a prescription or medical report under 6 months old and a passport copy. Some substances are banned outright.

notes: Ministry of Public Health guideline (Pharmacy and Drug Control Department): drugs banned internationally and locally, and those in Sub-schedules A and B of Schedule 1 of Law No. 9 of 1987, may not be released. Prohibited items include cannabis, cannabis resin, heroin, LSD, psilocybin, cathinone, MDA and dronabinol. For patients arriving for personal use you need: a detailed approved medical report or prescription no more than six months old, showing patient details, diagnosis, treatment plan and duration, recommendations, scientific drug name, form, dose and quantity, stamped and on the health facility's letterhead; a signed undertaking that only you will use it; and a passport copy. 'An amount of narcotic and psychoactive substances sufficient for a maximum of thirty days or the duration of the patient's stay in the State of Qatar, whichever is shorter, is allowed' and 'An amount of psychotropic substances sufficient for a maximum of two months is allowed'. Any excess is destroyed by the department. The narcotic/psychoactive list includes amfetamine, dexamfetamine, codeine, dihydrocodeine, fentanyl, hydrocodone, hydromorphone, methadone, morphine, oxycodone and pethidine. The psychotropic list includes alprazolam, bromazepam, buprenorphine, clonazepam, diazepam, lorazepam, midazolam, temazepam, zolpidem, phentermine, phenobarbital, tramadol, pregabalin and gabapentin. The guide tells you to check INCB's Yellow and Green lists for updates. Methylphenidate (Ritalin/Concerta) and lisdexamfetamine (Vyvanse) are not named on the lists, so they are not included in names here. Permit: MOPH's Controlled Medicines System (https://fli.moph.gov.qa/traveller/home; user manual v1.0, 2025) takes applications from travellers carrying narcotic/psychotropic medicines for personal use. You upload passport, prescription, medical report and photos of the medicine; applications are 'approved or rejected within three working days after all requirements have been met', and MOPH advises applying at least five working days before travel; an approved permit letter is 'valid for 90 days from date of approval' and 'must be printed and carried along with the original medical prescription and medical report during travel'. GOV.UK confirms the online permit system. The guideline PDF is dated Nov 2022; the controlling law is Law No. 9 of 1987.
summary: Needs a Ministry of Public Health permit: up to 30 days of narcotic medicines (or your stay, if shorter), or 2 months of psychotropics. Some are banned.

legal_source.name: Ministry of Public Health Qatar, Pharmacy and Drug Control Department — 'Controls and Regulations for the release of narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances and psychoactive drugs in the possession of patients arriving in or departing the State of Qatar' (Guideline of Controlled Drugs for Travellers, PDF)

procedure.title: Get a Controlled Medication Permit from Qatar's Ministry of Public Health
procedure.authority: Pharmacy and Drug Control Department, Ministry of Public Health
procedure.leadTime: At least 5 working days before you travel
procedure.processingTime: Approved or rejected within 3 working days once all requirements are met
documents: A copy of your passport (or Qatar ID).
The medical prescription.
The medical report.
Photos of the medicine.
steps: Register in Qatar's National Authentication System (NAS) with your passport number, mobile number and email, then log in to the Controlled Medicines System.
Create a request and complete the patient profile, plus anyone travelling with you.

Enter your trip (arrival, dates, port of entry, emergency contact) and each medicine: diagnosis, active ingredient, dosage form, prescription length in days, concentration, pack size, number of packs and trade name. You can add up to 5 active ingredients.
Upload the documents, accept the pledges and submit.
If approved, the system issues a permit letter with a permit number. It's valid for 90 days from approval; if you don't use it in time, apply again.
procedure.atTheBorder: Print the permit and carry it with the original prescription and medical report. The ministry can still release only part of the medicine, or refuse it, if it doesn't meet the approval criteria.

Your details, the diagnosis, the treatment plan and duration, and recommendations
The scientific drug name, form, dose and quantity

source.name: Ministry of Public Health Qatar, Pharmacy and Drug Control Department — 'Controls and Regulations for the release of narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances and psychoactive drugs in the possession of patients arriving in or departing the State of Qatar' (Guideline of Controlled Drugs for Travellers, PDF)

notes: Ministry of Public Health 'Items Prohibited from Entering the State of Qatar' (covering active raw materials or 'any pharmaceutical dosage forms i.e tablets, capsules, syrup, injection, oils, etc.') lists CANNABIS, CANNABIS RESIN and DRONABINOL (synthetic THC). Medical cannabis prescriptions do not make them allowed. The General Authority of Customs' list of goods forbidden by tariff also includes Cannabis sativa, Hashish and hemp seeds. GOV.UK: zero tolerance; possession of drugs 'including cannabis, (even residual amounts)' brings severe penalties, also in transit, and airports scan transit baggage. CBD is not named on any page read: CBD extracted from cannabis falls within 'cannabis … in any pharmaceutical dosage form … oils', but no source addresses hemp-derived CBD by name, so 'cbd' is not in names; ask MOPH before travelling with any CBD product.
summary: Banned: cannabis, cannabis resin and synthetic THC (dronabinol) are prohibited in Qatar, even with a medical prescription.

legal_source.name: Ministry of Public Health Qatar, Pharmacy and Drug Control Department — 'Controls and Regulations for the release of narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances and psychoactive drugs in the possession of patients arriving in or departing the State of Qatar' (Guideline of Controlled Drugs for Travellers, PDF)

transit.description: UK government travel advice says to expect a long prison sentence, deportation and heavy fines for possessing, using or smuggling illegal drugs, including cannabis and even residual amounts, "including when transiting through the airport". Qatar's airports scan transit passengers' baggage too.

notes: The General Authority of Customs' 'Goods forbidden by Tariff' list includes 'Electronic devices for cigarettes', 'Electronic water pipe "shisha"', 'Electrically heated devices for cigarettes' (heated-tobacco devices) and their parts. GOV.UK: 'It is illegal to import and sell vapes and electronic cigarette products. This includes the sale and purchase of related liquids and other similar products, including electronic shisha pipes. The law applies regardless of quantity and intended use. Customs officials may confiscate any such items from your luggage', and 'It is illegal to vape or use an e-cigarette. Police can arrest you and courts can impose a fine, a prison sentence or deportation.'
summary: Banned: e-cigarettes, e-liquids, heated-tobacco devices and electronic shisha can't be imported into Qatar, whatever the quantity.

limits.description: Up to 2,500 cc (2.5 litres) of alcoholic beverages per adult traveller duty-free as part of baggage.

notes: Aduana Exempt Resolution No. 309 (Annex 5, point I.3) includes in a traveller's duty-free baggage, per adult traveller, '2500 cubic centimeters of alcoholic beverages'. The joint Aduana–SAG declaration form states this applies to 'people over the age 18'. Anything above the allowance must be declared and taxed. Separately, duty-free shop purchases made on arrival in Chile (Law 19.288) are allowed up to US$675 per trip — Exempt Resolution No. 1301 raised this from US$500 (the older figure still printed on the 2016 declaration form and on some Aduana FAQ pages; the resolution controls). Aduana's 'Visto Bueno' list notes alcoholic beverages are an SAG-controlled product for imports generally; the baggage allowance above is the traveller rule.

legal_source.name: Servicio Nacional de Aduanas — Exempt Resolution No. 309 (Annex No. 5, Appendix XI, Chapter III of the Compendium of Customs Regulations: benefits for travellers; in force 13 March 2018), official English version; amounts updated by Exempt Resolution No. 1301

limits.description: Per adult traveller: 400 cigarettes, 500 g of pipe tobacco and 50 cigars, duty-free.

notes: Aduana Exempt Resolution No. 309 (Annex 5, point I.3): 'Up to a quantity not exceeding per adult traveler 400 units of cigarettes, 500 grams of pipe tobacco; 50 units of cigars'. The joint Aduana–SAG form gives the same figures for travellers over 18. Amounts above this must be declared and taxed. E-cigarettes are not mentioned in the allowance (see e-cigarettes, unverified).

legal_source.name: Servicio Nacional de Aduanas — Exempt Resolution No. 309 (Annex No. 5, Appendix XI, Chapter III of the Compendium of Customs Regulations: benefits for travellers; in force 13 March 2018), official English version; amounts updated by Exempt Resolution No. 1301

limits.description: Cash or bearer negotiable instruments over US$10,000 (or the equivalent in any currency, including Chilean pesos) must be declared to Aduanas on entry and on exit.

notes: Aduana 'Declaración de Dinero' page: 'Si ingresas o sales de Chile con más de US$ 10.000 o su equivalente en cualquier moneda debes declararlo ante Aduanas' (legal basis: art. 4 of Law 19.913); the same page's next sentence says 'desde 10.000 dólares' (from US$10,000) — so declaring at exactly US$10,000 is the safe choice. Declare to Aduana officials at the border checkpoint; the joint Aduana–SAG form has a yes/no box for it. Penalty: the current Aduana page quotes art. 168 bis of the Ordenanza de Aduanas — when the offence is detected Aduanas 'deberá retener la totalidad del dinero en efectivo o los instrumentos negociables al portador' and must bring criminal action immediately (the page links Law 21.632 strengthening anti-smuggling law). The older 2016 joint form instead describes a fine of up to 30% of the undeclared amount (Law 19.913 art. 39); the current Aduana page is treated as controlling and the conflict is noted.
summary: Declare cash or bearer instruments over US$10,000 (or the equivalent in any currency) to Customs when entering or leaving Chile.

legal_source.name: Servicio Nacional de Aduanas — Declaración de Dinero (Viajero, viajera y turista)

limits.description: Personal-use medicines in quantities consistent with the prescription (ISP's reference is up to 6 months of treatment), carried with a dated, doctor-signed prescription or medical certificate no older than 6 months; OTC medicines only in the amount needed for your stay.

notes: ISP 'Guía para ingresar medicamentos a Chile en el equipaje' (5 June 2025): Chile has no specific health regulation for medicines in travellers' baggage; the customs baggage rule covers 'Medicamentos, en cantidades conforme a la respectiva receta médica, siempre que sean para su uso personal o de familiares directos'; OTC medicines only in quantities for personal use. ISP requires: carry the prescription or medical certificate showing daily dose and length of treatment, 'idealmente traducida al español'; it must be dated, not more than 6 months old, and signed by a doctor; generic/INN name suggested; quantity consistent with the prescribed treatment ('el uso racional de medicamentos considera hasta seis (6) meses de tratamiento'); keep medicines in their original packaging; medicines must travel with the passenger. Raw materials ('polvos, líquidos o productos no etiquetados') are prohibited. Aduana: quantities that exceed normal personal use are presumed commercial and retained. Aduana's Visto Bueno page also notes ISP-related retention of products such as melatonin, slimming products and supplements claiming therapeutic properties, and hormonal supplements.
summary: Personal quantities with a signed prescription or medical certificate under 6 months old; ISP refers to up to 6 months of treatment.

legal_source.name: Instituto de Salud Pública de Chile (ISP), Agencia Nacional de Medicamentos — Guía para ingresar medicamentos a Chile en el equipaje (published 5 June 2025)

items: A prescription or medical certificate showing the daily dose and length of treatment
Dated, no more than 6 months old, and signed by a doctor
Ideally translated into Spanish, with the generic (INN) name

source.name: Instituto de Salud Pública de Chile (ISP), Agencia Nacional de Medicamentos — Guía para ingresar medicamentos a Chile en el equipaje (published 5 June 2025)

limits.description: No separate traveller procedure is published; ISP's general personal-use rule applies (prescription with dose and duration, quantity matching the treatment, original packaging), but possession of narcotic/psychotropic substances without justification is a crime under Law 20.000.

notes: ISP's traveller guide (5 June 2025) does not set a separate rule for narcotic or psychotropic medicines; it applies the general personal-use conditions to all medicines and cites the UNODC/INCB guidelines stating that travellers under medical treatment carrying internationally controlled medicines are not carrying out an import/export operation. Chile publishes no list of restricted medicines for travellers (the Korean Embassy in Chile, citing the ISP guide in Aug 2026, says Chile does not publish one). Legal backdrop (Law 20.000, version in force from 23 May 2026, bcn.cl): art. 3 treats importing or carrying such substances 'sin contar con la autorización competente' as trafficking; art. 4 punishes possession of small quantities 'a menos que justifique que están destinadas a la atención de un tratamiento médico' or exclusive, near-term personal use. So bring the prescription (Spanish translation recommended), only the prescribed quantity, in original packaging, and ask ISP (Agencia Nacional de Medicamentos) in advance if unsure. No specific drug (e.g. a named ADHD stimulant) is named by any source read, so none is named here.
summary: No separate traveller procedure: carry a prescription showing dose and duration, with the medicine in original packaging.

legal_source.name: Instituto de Salud Pública de Chile (ISP), Agencia Nacional de Medicamentos — Guía para ingresar medicamentos a Chile en el equipaje (published 5 June 2025)

limits.description: Prescription injectables follow the general personal-use rule: quantity consistent with a dated (≤6 months), doctor-signed prescription showing dose and duration, in original packaging.

notes: ISP's traveller guide (5 June 2025) applies one rule to all personal-use prescription medicines, so insulin and GLP-1 pens (e.g. Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro) are covered as prescription medicines: carry the prescription/medical certificate with daily dose and duration (ideally translated into Spanish), dated within 6 months and doctor-signed; quantity consistent with the treatment (reference: up to 6 months); original packaging. No source read addresses needles/syringes, sharps or cold-chain packaging specifically, and none names these brands — the names are listed only because they are prescription medicines within the general rule.
summary: Allowed in quantities matching a signed prescription under 6 months old, in original packaging.

legal_source.name: Instituto de Salud Pública de Chile (ISP), Agencia Nacional de Medicamentos — Guía para ingresar medicamentos a Chile en el equipaje (published 5 June 2025)

Dated within the last 6 months and signed by a doctor
Ideally translated into Spanish

source.name: Instituto de Salud Pública de Chile (ISP), Agencia Nacional de Medicamentos — Guía para ingresar medicamentos a Chile en el equipaje (published 5 June 2025)

notes: ISP's 2023 cannabis guide: 'Cannabis es Estupefaciente', THC is a psychotropic, and any cannabis extract with more than 0.2% THC is a narcotic; foods may not contain cannabis or derivatives; import of controlled cannabis raw material is allowed only for manufacturing pharmaceutical products. Aduana 'Viajeros que ingresan al país': 'En Chile, está prohibido y penado por ley la tenencia y el tráfico de drogas y sustancias psicotrópicas'. Law 20.000 art. 3 treats importing such substances without authorisation as trafficking. Law 20.000's medical-cannabis provision (art. 8, as quoted by ISP) concerns cultivation justified by a prescription from a treating doctor; nothing read authorises travellers to import cannabis. Do not bring cannabis or THC products, including medical cannabis prescribed abroad, without first checking with ISP.
summary: Banned: cannabis is a narcotic in Chile, and possessing or trafficking drugs is a crime.

legal_source.name: Instituto de Salud Pública de Chile — Cannabis: uso medicinal, vigilancia y control (Versión 2023); Ley N° 20.000 (latest version in force from 23 May 2026, Biblioteca del Congreso Nacional); Aduana — Viajeros que ingresan al país

limits.description: CBD products are treated as medicines; products with >0.2% THC are narcotics (prohibited); ISP has authorised no cannabis cosmetics and foods may not contain cannabis.

notes: ISP 2023 cannabis guide: 'Todo producto con cannabis y derivados es MEDICAMENTO'; cannabis extract with under 0.2% THC and CBD (cannabidiol) are pharmaceutical raw materials 'no sujetas a control legal' as narcotics, but 'Todo producto en base a extracto de cannabis que contenga un porcentaje mayor al 0,2 de THC es un estupefaciente'; 'El ISP no ha autorizado cosméticos con cannabis y derivados'; 'Los alimentos NO pueden contener cannabis y derivados' (hemp seed foods are subject to THC contaminant limits in DS 977/1966 art. 170 bis). No source read says whether a traveller may carry a CBD product for personal use. Treat CBD gummies, creams and oils as risky; check with ISP before travelling.
summary: CBD products count as medicines in Chile; anything over 0.2% THC is a narcotic. No cannabis cosmetics are authorised, and foods may not contain cannabis.

legal_source.name: Instituto de Salud Pública de Chile — Cannabis: uso medicinal, vigilancia y control (Versión 2023); Ley N° 20.000 (latest version in force from 23 May 2026, Biblioteca del Congreso Nacional); Aduana — Viajeros que ingresan al país

limits.description: All animal products must be declared on the joint Aduana–SAG sworn declaration; an SAG inspector decides whether each item may enter.

notes: SAG 'Ingreso a Chile' (page read 2026-10-10; sag.gob.cl itself was down for maintenance, read via sag.cl): every person entering Chile must declare under oath any animal or plant products carried 'sin importar su cantidad o tiempo desde que lo obtuvo'; 'Un/a inspector/a SAG evaluará si el producto está en condiciones de ingresar al país'. The joint Aduana–SAG form lists animal products to declare: live animals (birds, bees, pets), 'Carne o derivados (jamón, embutidos, otros)', 'Leche y sus derivados (queso, yogurt, otros)', bee products (honey, royal jelly, propolis), veterinary medicines, semen/embryos, animal feed, 'Productos de origen animal y comida de uso personal, que los contenga', animal-origin crafts (antlers, horns, hooves), trophies and insect collections; CITES species need documentation. 'Declaring YES does not necessarily imply authorization'; a false SAG declaration 'constituye falta y será sancionado con multa' (no amount verified — see unverified). Luggage may be X-rayed or checked by SAG detector dogs. Which specific products are refused was not readable (SAG product pages unavailable), so the verdict is declaration rather than a ban.

legal_source.name: Servicio Agrícola y Ganadero (SAG) — Ingreso a Chile: declara todos los productos vegetales y animales que traigas a Chile

limits.description: All plant products — fresh, dried, dehydrated, frozen or processed — must be declared on the joint Aduana–SAG sworn declaration; an SAG inspector decides whether each item may enter.

notes: SAG 'Ingreso a Chile': declare every plant or animal product regardless of quantity; an SAG inspector decides admissibility. The joint Aduana–SAG form lists plant products to declare: 'Frutos y hortalizas (frescas, secas, deshidratadas, congeladas y agroindustrializadas)', live plants and plant parts, all grains and seeds (including for eating), legumes, spices/herbs/seasonings, flowers, soil or anything containing soil, plant-origin crafts, wood, conifer cones, biological material (live insects, spores), other packed or unpacked plant products, pesticides and fertilisers. False declaration is punishable by a fine. Declaring does not guarantee entry; non-compliant products are not allowed in.
summary: Declare all plant products on the SAG sworn declaration; an inspector decides what may enter.

limits.description: Firearms, ammunition, explosives and martial-arts implements (including bows, arrows, crossbows) need prior DGMN authorisation; foreign hunters and sport shooters apply for a temporary-import authorisation through a Chilean legal representative.

notes: Aduana 'Productos que requieren autorización o Visto Bueno': 'Armas de fuego, municiones, explosivos y sustancias químicas, inflamables y asfixiantes e implementos de artes marciales' require the Visto Bueno of the Dirección General de Movilización Nacional (DGMN); 'Los implementos para la realización de Artes Marciales ... requieren permisos de la DGMN, dentro de ellos arcos, flechas y ballestas, keibo, cadenas con puntas metálicas'. ChileAtiende/DGMN 'Autorización para la internación temporal de armas' (Ley 17.798; Decreto 83): available to foreign hunters, shooting federations and clubs, sportspeople, exhibitors and embassies; for hunting a legal representative must file a notarised document taking responsibility for the weapons while in Chile; applied for at DGMN offices; reply within 20 working days; validity 'En caso necesario, 180 días'; fee per DGMN schedule (amount not shown). Bringing a weapon without authorisation is an offence.
summary: Firearms, ammunition, explosives, bows and crossbows need prior DGMN authorisation.

legal_source.name: ChileAtiende / Dirección General de Movilización Nacional (DGMN) — Autorización para la internación temporal de armas (Ley N° 17.798; Decreto N° 83)

limits.description: No customs ban was found; flying is regulated by DGAC. Over populated areas DAN 151 requires DGAC registration, a remote-pilot credential and an operating authorisation; key limits: max 120 m (400 ft), visual line of sight, not within 2 km of a runway axis extension or 1 km parallel to a runway, never over military sites or prisons.

notes: DGAC DAN 151 Ed. 3 (May 2024) applies to anyone operating an RPA 'sobre áreas pobladas' for public-interest matters or aerial work, alongside DAN 91 'Reglas del Aire'. It requires: prior DGAC authorisation (151.101) with the RPA registration card, the remote-pilot credential, insurance, a KMZ of the site and the landowner's permission; registration in the DGAC RPA registry (151.201, the application form asks for a Chilean ID card/RUT); a credential requiring age 18+ and a written exam (151.303); max take-off weight 9 kg and an emergency parachute (151.005). Operating limits (151.103): VLOS only, max 500 m distance and 400 ft (120 m) height, not within 2 km of the runway extension or 1 km parallel to a runway, no prohibited/dangerous zones, no night flights without authorisation, one RPA at a time. 151.105: all flights over military installations, prisons and strategic installations are prohibited. Rules for purely recreational flying over unpopulated areas (DAN 91) and whether a tourist can register a drone were not confirmed — check with DGAC before flying. Aduana treats radio-transmitting equipment as needing SUBTEL authorisation in general imports; not confirmed for traveller drones.

notes: Montenegrin Customs Administration instruction (31 Oct 2025) applying Articles 8–9 of the Decree on exemption from import duties (Sl. list CG 31/25). People under 17 get no alcohol or tobacco allowance. The alcohol/tobacco quantities are duty-free regardless of value and are not counted toward the general goods allowance (EUR 430 for air and sea travellers, EUR 300 for other travellers, EUR 150 for under-15s). Above the allowance, full import duties are charged (up to the maximum quantities of excise goods individuals may import). Goods must be occasional and for personal/family use or gifts, not commercial.

Arriving by any OTHER means (land, sea, rail): only 40 cigarettes, or 20 cigarillos, or 10 cigars, or 50 g smoking tobacco.

notes: Customs Administration instruction of 31 Oct 2025 (Decree Sl. list CG 31/25, Art. 8 for air travel, Art. 9 for 'other types of traffic'). The lower allowance for non-air arrivals is a common surprise for travellers driving in from Croatia, Bosnia, Serbia or Albania or arriving by ferry. Under-17s get no tobacco allowance. Tobacco above the allowance is charged full import duties.
summary: By air: 200 cigarettes or equivalent. By land or sea: only 40 cigarettes or equivalent.

legal_source.name: Oslobođenje od plaćanja uvoznih dažbina na robu u ličnom prtljagu — Customs Administration of Montenegro (Uprava carina) instruction no. 14388/1-25 of 31 Oct 2025, applying the Decree on conditions and procedure for exemption from import duties (Sl. list CG 31/25)

limits.description: You must declare to customs, on entry and on exit, cash of EUR 10,000 or more (or the equivalent in other currencies), and the same applies to cheques, bearer securities, precious metals and precious stones of that value. Customs ask for full documentation on where the money came from.

notes: Customs Administration operational notice no. D-6425/1-25 of 8 May 2025: anyone carrying 'novac, čekovi, hartije od vrijednosti na donosioca, dragocjeni metali ili drago kamenje' worth EUR 10,000 or more across the border must declare it to customs and provide complete documentation on its origin. If undeclared money has no sign of illegal origin it is not seized, but a misdemeanour penalty order is issued. If there is suspicion about its origin (declared or not, and at any amount), customs may hold the money and the person for up to 6 hours while the police Financial Intelligence Unit and prosecutor decide. The Customs Administration's 2016 instruction (also published on the same page) cites the legal basis as Art. 10 of the Law on Current and Capital Transactions with Foreign Countries and the Decision setting EUR 10,000 as the limit for carrying cash without declaring it, and gives a fine of EUR 550–2,000 for individuals (that figure is from 2016 and may have changed). UK FCDO advice agrees: declare cash or travellers' cheques of EUR 10,000 or more, keep the certified declaration, or the money may be seized when you leave.
summary: Declare €10,000 or more in cash, cheques, bearer securities or precious metals on entry and exit.

legal_source.name: Obavještenje o operativnom postupanju na graničnim prelazima u vezi sa prenosom sredstava plaćanja — Customs Administration of Montenegro (Uprava carina), 8 May 2025

limits.description: You may bring a reasonable amount of medication for your personal use, up to a maximum of 6 months' supply. Medicines containing narcotic or controlled substances have stricter rules (30 days' supply, doctor's certificate, declare) — see the controlled-medication row.

notes: UK FCDO: 'When travelling to Montenegro, you may carry a reasonable amount of medication needed for personal use for a maximum of 6 months.' Montenegro's customs Decree (Sl. list CG 31/25, Art. 7) also provides that the value of medicines and medical devices necessary for the traveller's personal needs is not counted toward the duty-free value limit. The 6-month figure comes from the UK government page; we did not find it in a Montenegrin legal text. Keep medicines in original packaging with your prescription.

legal_source.name: Montenegro travel advice — Entry requirements (UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office, GOV.UK)

limits.description: You may carry a medicine containing a controlled drug only in the amount needed for your own treatment for at most 30 days, and you must carry a certificate (report) from your doctor confirming you need it. The certificate may not be older than 90 days. The UK government also says to declare such medicine to customs on arrival.
limits.quantity: Max 30 days' supply + doctor's certificate under 90 days old

notes: Law on Prevention of Drug Abuse, Art. 43: 'Lice koje prelazi državnu granicu može da posjeduje lijek koji sadrži drogu u količini potrebnoj za ličnu terapiju, za period od najviše 30 dana na osnovu potvrde (izvještaja) izabranog doktora ili doktora medicine specijaliste...' and 'Potvrda o neophodnosti posjedovanja lijeka ne može biti starija od 90 dana.' The same rule (30 days, certificate from a vet, under 90 days old) applies to medicine for an animal travelling with you, and for that the law expressly requires reporting the certificate to customs (fine EUR 100 if not, Art. 52a). For human medicine the law requires you to carry the certificate; UK FCDO advice additionally says 'You must declare any prescription medication containing narcotics to customs on arrival' and that undocumented or undeclared medication 'may lead to confiscation and legal action' — declaring is the safe course. Holding more than the doctor-prescribed amount is a misdemeanour (EUR 100–2,000, Art. 52). The law does not name specific medicines; whether a given medicine is covered depends on Montenegro's official list of drugs and psychotropic substances, which we did not review. The Ministry's own 2020 traveller notice (gov.me article 222598, now archived) states the same rule.
summary: Up to 30 days' supply, with a doctor's certificate no older than 90 days.

legal_source.name: Zakon o sprječavanju zloupotrebe droga (Law on Prevention of Drug Abuse, Sl. list CG 28/11, 35/13) — consolidated text published by the Government of Montenegro

items: A certificate (report) from your chosen doctor or a specialist confirming you need the medicine
No older than 90 days
Covering at most 30 days of your treatment

source.name: Zakon o sprječavanju zloupotrebe droga (Law on Prevention of Drug Abuse, Sl. list CG 28/11, 35/13) — consolidated text published by the Government of Montenegro

limits.description: Using, producing, trading or possessing drugs for personal use is prohibited. Do not bring cannabis into Montenegro.

notes: Law on Prevention of Drug Abuse, Art. 45: 'Zabranjena je upotreba, proizvodnja, promet, posjedovanje droga za ličnu upotrebu...' Possessing drugs for personal use is a misdemeanour fined EUR 100–2,000 (Art. 52); larger amounts and trafficking are criminal offences. UK FCDO: 'Illegal drugs, including cannabis, carry severe penalties.' Not covered here: CBD products and any Montenegrin medical-cannabis rules — we found no primary source on those, so don't assume CBD is allowed.
summary: Banned: using, trading or possessing drugs, even for personal use, is prohibited in Montenegro.

legal_source.name: Zakon o sprječavanju zloupotrebe droga (Law on Prevention of Drug Abuse, Sl. list CG 28/11, 35/13) — consolidated text published by the Government of Montenegro

limits.description: You cannot bring meat, milk or products containing them into Montenegro. Exceptions: powdered baby milk, baby food, and special foods required for medical reasons (sealed, labelled, not needing special storage).

notes: UK FCDO: 'You cannot take meat, milk or products containing them into Montenegro. There are some exceptions such as powdered baby milk, baby food and special foods or pet feed required for medical reasons.' This matches the Ministry of Agriculture rulebook on food travellers bring into Montenegro (Sl. list CG 27/2008, Art. 4–5), which lists meat, meat products, fish, molluscs, milk and dairy products, eggs, animal fat, gelatin and collagen as not allowed without a veterinary certificate, and allows powdered milk/baby food and medically required food; and up to 1 kg of heat-treated (canned) pet food (Art. 8). We read that rulebook only via the FAO legal database copy and could not confirm it is still in force, so the cited source is the current UK page. Items that don't meet the rules are seized and destroyed at the border.
summary: Banned: meat, milk and products containing them. Exceptions: powdered baby milk, baby food and medically required foods, sealed and labelled.

legal_source.name: Montenegro travel advice — Entry requirements (UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office, GOV.UK)

limits.description: Visitors without permanent residence may bring hunting or sporting firearms and ammunition only to hunt or take part in sports competitions (or cultural events), and the weapon must be entered in your passport (by a Montenegrin embassy/consulate, or by the border police if you hold a licence to carry it in your home country). Declare it to the border police on arrival with your weapon document and proof of purpose (invitation letter, hunt or competition organiser's notice). Cross only at international border crossings, and you may not sell the weapon.

notes: Law on Weapons and Ammunition (Zakon o oružju i municiji), adopted 31 July 2026 and proclaimed 3 August 2026, which replaces the 2015 Law on Weapons: Art. 66 (foreigners without permanent residence may carry weapons across the border for hunting, sports competitions and cultural events, only at international crossings, and may not sell them), Art. 67 (must declare weapons and ammunition to the border police and show the weapon document and proof of purpose), Art. 72 (hunting/sporting weapons must be entered in the travel document; the border police issues an entry approval and cancels it on exit). Art. 75 (EU European Firearms Pass) applies only from Montenegro's EU accession. Other weapon types (self-defence weapons, knives, pepper spray, replicas) were not researched — treat them as not covered.
summary: Hunting or sporting firearms only for hunts or competitions, entered in your passport and declared to border police.

legal_source.name: Zakon o oružju i municiji (Law on Weapons and Ammunition), Službeni list Crne Gore, 2026

limits.description: Bringing a drone is not restricted by customs rules we found, but flying is regulated. Near Podgorica and Tivat airports, flying inside the restricted areas around each airport needs prior approval from Montenegro's Airspace Management Cell (AMC), applied for at least two working days ahead (by 10:00 UTC) for each flight. Elsewhere inside the Podgorica and Tivat control zones you may fly up to 50 m above ground; 50–120 m needs AMC approval.

notes: Civil Aviation Agency of Montenegro Safety Order 2017/001 rev 03 (based on the Law on Air Transport and the Rulebook on safe use of unmanned aircraft systems, Sl. list CG 24/23 and 117/23). The Agency's unmanned-aircraft page lists this as revision 3, published 1 July 2024. Not verified here: Montenegro's general drone registration, operator/pilot training (an A1/A3 theory course is offered by the Agency) and rules outside the two airport control zones under Rulebook 24/23 — check caa.me before flying.
summary: Flying near Podgorica and Tivat airports needs Airspace Management Cell approval; elsewhere in their zones, up to 50 m.

legal_source.name: Safety Order 2017/001 rev 03 laying down requirements for use of unmanned aircraft systems within CTR Podgorica and CTR Tivat — Civil Aviation Agency of Montenegro

limits.description: Travellers aged 18+ may bring 1 litre of spirits and 1 litre of wine duty-free (the stricter of two official figures; the Customs FAQ says 2 litres of alcoholic beverages). Declare anything above this.

notes: Two official Jamaica Customs Agency (JCA) figures differ. The JCA FAQ (live page, no date shown) says 'All passengers, 18 years and over, are allowed the following without payment of duty, provided they do not exceed the amount indicated, and the items are properly declared: … Alcoholic beverages .. 2 litres'. The official Immigration/Customs C5 card (JCA PDF, 2020 upload, https://jca.gov.jm/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/C5new.x11699.pdf) says passengers and crew may import free of duty '1 litre of Spirits; 1 litre of Wine'. Both add up to 2 litres, but the C5 splits it by type, so the stricter reading (no more than 1 litre of spirits) is shown. Bringing alcohol in bulk is a matter for the Spirits Pool Association (JCA Prohibited & Restricted Items guide). Goods over your allowance must be declared on the C5 and you use the red line.
summary: Travellers 18+: 1 litre of spirits and 1 litre of wine duty-free. Declare anything above that.

legal_source.name: What are my duty-free allowances and exemptions? — Jamaica Customs Agency FAQ

limits.description: Travellers aged 18+ may bring 200 cigarettes, or 50 cigars, or 230 g of processed tobacco duty-free.

notes: JCA FAQ: all passengers 18 years and over may bring without duty 'Tobacco (sticks) …….200 cigarettes,50 cigars or 230 grams of processed tobacco', provided the items are properly declared and within the amount. The C5 card gives the same: '200 sticks of cigarettes or 50 sticks of cigars or 230g of Tobacco'. The allowance is one of the three, not all three. E-cigarettes are not covered by this allowance (see the unverified e-cigarette entry).

legal_source.name: What are my duty-free allowances and exemptions? — Jamaica Customs Agency FAQ

limits.description: Declare cash or monetary instruments over US$10,000 (or equivalent in any currency) on the C5 form; you must be able to show the money's source and purpose.

notes: JCA press release (13 October 2025): 'while carrying cash across borders is not illegal, travellers must declare any amount over US$10,000 (or its equivalent) and must be able to verify its source and purpose.' The C5 card, question 14: 'I am carrying currency or monetary instruments over US$10,000 or equivalent'. The UK government's advice (https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/jamaica/entry-requirements) phrases it as 'Declare cash or travellers cheques if the value is 10,000 US dollars or more', on the C5, and says you will also complete the Financial Investigation Division Cross Border Form provided by a customs officer — so declare at exactly US$10,000 too, to be safe. Separately, Section 101A of the Proceeds of Crime Act prohibits cash payments of J$1,000,000 or more in Jamaica (two travellers were fined J$200,000 each in 2025 under that section). The C5 states failure to make a full declaration is an offence that may result in fines, forfeiture and/or imprisonment. Spain's embassy also lists importing local currency (Jamaican dollars) among prohibited imports (exteriores.gob.es, June 2026) — not confirmed on a JCA page.

legal_source.name: Joint enforcement at NMIA leads to POCA convictions; travellers fined after declaring large cash sums — Jamaica Customs Agency press release, 13 October 2025

limits.description: Regular (non-narcotic) prescription medicine for your stay is allowed if it is in its original labelled containers and you carry a copy of every prescription (name, quantity, strength, dosage) plus a doctor's letter stating the condition treated.

notes: Embassy of Jamaica, Brussels (Ministry of Health and Wellness guidance, page © 2026): 'Travellers to Jamaica may bring regular prescriptions to Jamaica for use during their stay in Jamaica provided that: The person brings a copy of all prescriptions clearly stating name, the quantity, strength and dosage and that all the prescription drugs are in the original containers and clearly labelled. Letter from the physician stating the condition being treated.' Prescriptions containing narcotics need a special Ministry of Health permit (see controlled-medication-jm). The C5 card asks you to declare pharmaceuticals in commercial quantities, and the JCA Prohibited & Restricted Items guide lists pharmaceuticals under the Ministry of Health & Wellness. Spain's embassy (exteriores.gob.es, June 2026) likewise says medicines must travel in their original packaging with the doctor's prescription.
summary: Allowed in original labelled containers, with a copy of each prescription and a doctor's letter.

legal_source.name: Importation of Prescription Drugs to Jamaica — Embassy of Jamaica and Jamaica Mission to the EU, Brussels (reproducing Ministry of Health and Wellness guidance)

items: A copy of every prescription, clearly stating your name, the quantity, strength and dosage
A letter from your physician stating the condition being treated

source.name: Importation of Prescription Drugs to Jamaica — Embassy of Jamaica and Jamaica Mission to the EU, Brussels (reproducing Ministry of Health and Wellness guidance)

limits.description: Prescriptions containing narcotics need a special permit from Jamaica's Ministry of Health and Wellness, issued before you travel and carried with you.

notes: Embassy of Jamaica, Brussels (Ministry of Health and Wellness guidance): 'A special permit will be required from the Ministry of Health and Wellness for prescription containing narcotics.' Apply to the Chief Dangerous Drugs Inspector, Pharmaceutical and Regulatory Affairs Division, Ministry of Health and Wellness, 45-47 Barbados Avenue, Kingston 5 (tel. (876) 633-7145; 'Emailed requests will be accepted'). Send: a physician's letter with the patient's name and condition; a copy of the prescription with name, strength and quantity for the whole stay; flight details (dates/times, flight numbers, ports of entry and departure); your address in Jamaica; your contact details; and the physician's phone number. 'Once approval is granted, the Ministry of Health will directly send the applicant the special permit … This document must be carried with the patient when traveling to Jamaica.' No processing time is stated, so apply early. The source says 'narcotics' and names no specific drugs; it does not say whether non-narcotic controlled psychotropics (e.g. ADHD stimulants, benzodiazepines) need the same permit — ask the Pharmaceutical and Regulatory Affairs Division before travelling with any controlled medicine.

legal_source.name: Importation of Prescription Drugs to Jamaica — Embassy of Jamaica and Jamaica Mission to the EU, Brussels (reproducing Ministry of Health and Wellness guidance)

procedure.title: Get a special permit from Jamaica's Ministry of Health and Wellness
procedure.authority: Chief Dangerous Drugs Inspector, Pharmaceutical and Regulatory Affairs Division, Ministry of Health and Wellness
documents: A letter from your doctor giving your name and the condition being treated.
A copy of the prescription showing each drug's name, strength and quantity for your whole stay.
Your flight details: arrival and departure dates and times, flight numbers, and ports of entry and departure.
Your address in Jamaica, and your own address, phone number and email.
A phone number for your doctor.
steps: Gather the documents.
Send the request to the Chief Dangerous Drugs Inspector, 45-47 Barbados Avenue, Kingston 5 (tel. (876) 633-7145). Emailed requests are accepted. No processing time is stated, so apply early.
The ministry sends the special permit to you directly before your departure date.
procedure.atTheBorder: Carry the special permit with you when you travel to Jamaica.

sources.name: Importation of Prescription Drugs to Jamaica — Embassy of Jamaica and Jamaica Mission to the EU, Brussels (reproducing Ministry of Health and Wellness guidance)

limits.description: Do not bring cannabis into Jamaica. Small-amount possession inside Jamaica is a ticketable offence, and visitors can get a permit to buy medical ganja locally, but crossing the border with it is not allowed outside a narrow, regulated route for terminal or serious chronic illness.

notes: Ministry of Justice fact sheet on the Dangerous Drugs (Amendment) Act 2015: possession of 2 ounces or less is no longer an arrestable offence but police may issue a ticket (J$500, payable within 30 days); possession of over 2 ounces remains a criminal offence. Import: 'A person who is suffering from cancer or any other terminal or serious chronic illness may import medicine or a therapeutic product derived from or containing ganja' if a registered medical practitioner certifies the illness and recommends its use, and 'The importation … must comply with regulations which are to be made' — this route is not open to ordinary travellers. Visitors: 'Persons who do not ordinarily reside in Jamaica (for example, tourists …) may apply for a permit to allow them to lawfully purchase and possess up to 2 ounces of ganja at a time, for medical or therapeutic purposes', with evidence of a home-country medical recommendation or a voluntary declaration; 'The permit is issued by Jamaica's Ministry of Health, and a fee is payable' (the fact sheet is undated; the Cannabis Licensing Authority site was not checked). Government of Canada (https://travel.gc.ca/destinations/jamaica, 26 May 2026): 'Do not attempt to enter or depart Jamaica and cross international borders with any amount of cannabis.' GOV.UK: 'It's illegal to smoke marijuana (ganja) in Jamaica' and severe penalties apply to other drug offences including attempting to export narcotics. The C5 card asks you to declare illicit drugs or narcotics. CBD: hemp (under 1% THC) is excluded from the DDA ganja provisions but its import is to be regulated by the Cannabis Licensing Authority — no traveller rule for CBD products was found, so treat CBD as not confirmed allowed.
summary: Banned: you can't bring cannabis into Jamaica, even though small amounts are decriminalised locally.

legal_source.name: Dangerous Drugs (Amendment) Act 2015 — Fact Sheet Booklet, Ministry of Justice, Government of Jamaica

limits.description: Do not bring meat (raw, cooked or processed) or milk products without an import permit from the Ministry of Agriculture's Veterinary Services Division; customs may destroy them.

notes: JCA Prohibited & Restricted Items guide (March 2025): 'All meat imports, regardless of type or quantity, require an import permit from the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries'; the Veterinary Services Division list covers 'Meat (Raw or Cooked)', 'Milk & its by-products', 'Pet & Animal Foods' and 'Processed Meats & Sausages' (contact: (876) 977-2489, vsdpermits@micaf.gov.jm). UK government advice (https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/jamaica/entry-requirements): 'It is illegal to bring meat and dairy products into Jamaica. Customs officials may search your baggage and will destroy banned foodstuffs.' Spain's embassy also lists 'productos cárnicos' and honey as prohibited imports. The C5 card requires you to declare meat, food and animal products (question 13a). Shown as prohibited because a visitor without a prior permit cannot lawfully bring these in.
summary: Meat and milk products need a Veterinary Services import permit; otherwise customs may destroy them.

legal_source.name: Prohibited & Restricted Items guide — Jamaica Customs Agency (March 2025)

limits.description: Honey is a prohibited import.

notes: JCA Prohibited & Restricted Items guide (March 2025), under the Ministry of Agriculture & Fisheries (Plant Quarantine): 'Honey (Prohibited Item)'. Spain's embassy in Kingston (exteriores.gob.es, June 2026) also lists 'miel' among prohibited imports. Honey is also listed on the C5 card's declaration question 13a.

legal_source.name: Prohibited & Restricted Items guide — Jamaica Customs Agency (March 2025)

limits.description: Fresh fruit, vegetables, plants, plant products and ground provisions need an import permit from the Ministry of Agriculture's Plant Quarantine Division; declare them on the C5.

notes: JCA Prohibited & Restricted Items guide (March 2025): 'Importing agricultural items can unknowingly bring along harmful pests and diseases … these items are restricted and require a permit from the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries.' Plant Quarantine list: 'Fresh Fruits & Vegetables', 'Plants & Plant products', 'Red Peas (in commercial quantities)', 'Ground Provisions', 'Honey (Prohibited Item)' (contact: Plant Quarantine Division, (876) 977-0637). The C5 card question 13a requires declaring fruits, plants, cut flowers, vegetables, soil, plant material and food. Without a permit, expect such items to be refused or confiscated. The guide says it is not exhaustive and the list may change.
summary: Fresh fruit, vegetables and plants need a Plant Quarantine import permit; declare them on the C5 form.

legal_source.name: Prohibited & Restricted Items guide — Jamaica Customs Agency (March 2025)

limits.description: Do not bring firearms, ammunition or other listed weapons (including toy guns, pepper spray, tasers, swords, bows) without permits obtained in advance from the Trade Board and/or the Ministry of National Security.

notes: JCA Prohibited & Restricted Items guide (March 2025): firearms, explosives and fireworks are controlled by The Trade Board Limited; the Ministry of National Security (Protective Security & Small Arms Branch, protective.security@mns.gov.jm) controls 'Firearm Parts', 'Firearm Holsters', 'Ammunition', 'Bullet Proof Vests', 'Toy Guns', 'Bows & Arrows', 'Pepper Sprays', 'Taser / Stun Gun', 'Tactical Flashlights', 'Night Vision Goggles', 'Swords / Spears', 'Firearm Cleaning Kits', 'Handcuffs' and 'Camouflage Clothing & Materials'. On toy guns: 'importing any toy gun requires a permit from the Ministry of National Security.' Government of Canada (https://travel.gc.ca/destinations/jamaica): 'Entering the country with a firearm or even a single round of ammunition is considered a serious crime.' The C5 card requires declaring 'Arms ammunition, explosives, fireworks, toy guns or other weapons'. Shown as prohibited for ordinary travellers; the permit route exists but must be completed before arrival.
summary: Firearms, toy guns, pepper spray, tasers, swords and bows need permits in advance from the Trade Board or Ministry of National Security.

legal_source.name: Prohibited & Restricted Items guide — Jamaica Customs Agency (March 2025)

limits.description: Camouflage clothing and materials (and denim resembling police uniform) are restricted to military/police use; do not pack them.

notes: JCA Prohibited & Restricted Items guide (March 2025): 'Importing camouflage clothing and denim similar to the apparel of the Jamaica Constabulary Force is restricted in Jamaica. This type of apparel is reserved for military personnel only. Wearing of this type of apparel can be mistaken for impersonation of the Jamaica Defense Force or the Jamaica Constabulary Force.' 'Camouflage Clothing & Materials' are listed under the Ministry of National Security. Shown as prohibited because there is no visitor permit route described.

legal_source.name: Prohibited & Restricted Items guide — Jamaica Customs Agency (March 2025)

limits.description: Recreational drone flying needs no JCAA permit but strict rules apply (max 400 ft, within 500 m and line of sight, not within 5 km of aerodromes, no night/FPV flights). Any non-recreational use (e.g. paid photography) needs a JCAA Special Aerial Work Permit. Customs/radio-equipment rules for bringing a drone in were not confirmed.

notes: Jamaica Civil Aviation Authority, 'Unmanned Aircraft' (jcaa.gov.jm/unmanned-aircraft/): 'Professional operators, whether commercial or non-commercial, require a Special Aerial Work Permit from the JCAA … Recreational operators do not require a permit but must comply with the relevant operating guidelines.' Recreational guidelines (this page): not above 400 feet (122 m); not beyond 1,640 feet (500 m) or the operator's unaided visual range; no First-Person View; not over or within 500 ft (152 m) of an open-air assembly or 165 ft (50 m) of any person; not over private or public property without permission; not in restricted/prohibited airspace; not within 16,500 ft (5,000 m) of any aerodrome or helipad; must have fail-safe return/land; no autonomous flights, no night or low-visibility flights, no dropping items. Contact: Flight Safety Division, 876 960-3948, uavrequests@jcaa.gov.jm. NOT CONFIRMED: whether Jamaica Customs requires an import permit or Spectrum Management Authority type approval for a visitor's personal drone (radio equipment) — no official page addressing travellers was found, hence 'depends'. Check with JCA/SMA before travelling.

legal_source.name: Recreational UA Operators or Hobbyists — Jamaica Civil Aviation Authority

limits.description: Each adult may bring duty-free one quart of spirits and one quart of wine. Anything more is dutiable. Customs sets no separate duty-free beer allowance.
limits.quantity: 1 quart spirits + 1 quart wine per adult

notes: Bahamas Customs 'Arriving': 'DUTY FREE ALLOWANCES FOR ALL TRAVELLERS — Alcoholic Beverages not exceeding one quart of spirits and one quart of wine (Adults only)'. The General Traveler's Questions page (2 Jan 2026) repeats this for 'every traveling adult, either visitor or resident', 'in addition to the entitled exemption' (visitors: $100.00 per trip on any dutiable article; above that, duties and taxes apply). A quart is about 0.95 litres. Beer: Customs names no beer allowance; the Bahamas Ministry of Tourism site (cross-check only) says 'All beer imported into the country is dutiable at a rate of $10 per imperial gallon or $18 per case' — so plan to pay duty on beer. Visitors carrying only used personal belongings give an oral declaration; anyone carrying other items completes the C17 Baggage Declaration in the Exempt app, with receipts.

legal_source.name: The Bahamas Customs Department — Visitors: Arriving (duty-free allowances for all travellers)

limits.description: Each adult may bring duty-free one of: 200 cigarettes, OR 50 cigars, OR one pound (about 454 g) of tobacco.
limits.quantity: 200 cigarettes or 50 cigars or 1 lb tobacco

notes: Bahamas Customs 'Arriving': 'Tobacco not exceeding one pound in weight or 200 cigarettes or 50 cigars (Adults Only).' The allowance is in addition to the visitor's $100 exemption on dutiable goods. The source says 'Adults only' but does not state the age.

legal_source.name: The Bahamas Customs Department — Visitors: Arriving (duty-free allowances for all travellers)

limits.description: Declare cash and negotiable instruments worth BSD 10,000 (= USD 10,000) or more. This applies on arrival and on departure. The same threshold covers precious metals in bullion, and loose stones or jewellery carried for trade.

notes: Bahamas Customs General Traveler's Questions (2 Jan 2026), Q6 'Must I declare how much cash I am carrying?': 'Any person carrying cash and negotiable instruments of a value equivalent to $10,000.00 or more, loose or uncut precious stones or jewelery with intention to trade of a value equivalent to $10,000.00 or more; and precious metals in bullion'. 'Cash' includes coins and bank notes in any currency; 'Negotiable Instruments' includes cheques, travellers cheques, promissory notes, money orders and instruments in bearer form. On departure, the Customs 'Departing' page (Travellers Currency Declaration) says each person or responsible family member must declare cash, negotiable instruments, precious metals or stones 'of a value equivalent to BS $10,000.00'. 'Penalties for non-compliance can include forfeiture of the cash, plus up to a $2,000 fine.' Cross-check: Government of Canada travel advice says 'It's illegal to leave The Bahamas with more than 10,000 BSD.' The official tourism site says the Bahamian dollar 'is maintained at the same level as the U.S. dollar'.

legal_source.name: The Bahamas Customs Department — General Traveler's Questions (updated 2 Jan 2026)

notes: Official Bahamas visitor guidance (Ministry of Tourism FAQ, health and safety tips): 'The purchase and usage of marijuana is illegal and enforced with strict penalties.' Do not bring cannabis in any form. A foreign medical-cannabis card does not let you import it. Cross-checks: Auswärtiges Amt says drug use and trafficking, 'auch in geringsten Mengen' (even in the smallest amounts), are prosecuted very strictly, with heavy fines and prison and usually no bail. GOV.UK says 'Penalties for possessing or trafficking drugs are severe'. Legislative context: the Cannabis Act, 2024 was published in the Extraordinary Official Gazette (26 July 2024). It creates a licensed medical/religious cannabis regime, including a provision that 'A pharmacist may dispense medical cannabis to a visitor' who holds a medical card from a recognised jurisdiction and a prescription. It also contains a section titled 'Unlawful import and export of cannabis' (s.58). We could not confirm that the visitor-dispensing scheme is in operation, and nothing in it allows a traveller to bring their own supply. CBD: no official source addresses CBD separately, so this row doesn't cover CBD products.
summary: Banned: buying and using marijuana is illegal in the Bahamas, and a foreign medical-cannabis card doesn't let you bring it in.

legal_source.name: The Islands of The Bahamas official tourism site (bahamas.com, Bahamas Ministry of Tourism) — Frequently Asked Questions: health and safety tips

limits.description: Declare all food. Some dairy items are restricted. Meat and other food unfit for human consumption is prohibited.

notes: Bahamas Customs General Traveler's Questions (2 Jan 2026), Q14 'Can I bring food as a traveler?': 'Yes, you are allowed to travel with certain foods. There are restrictions when importing fruits, vegetables and some dairy items ... to prevent the introduction of certain diseases that are contracted from plants and animals. You must declare all food products. Failure to declare food products can result in forfeiture and or fines.' Customs' prohibited list includes 'Meat, provisions, fruits and vegetables, and any articles intended for human food, which are unfit for human consumption.' Customs gives no item-by-item list of which meat or dairy products are allowed. Separate Animal Contagious Diseases orders (meat, poultry and live-bird import prohibitions) exist on laws.bahamas.gov.bs, but we have not reviewed their current scope, so declare every meat, poultry or dairy item and expect it may be refused. The Bahamas Agricultural Health and Food Safety Authority (BAHFSA) site did not respond during research.

limits.description: Every drone must be registered with the Civil Aviation Authority Bahamas (CAA-B) before you fly. Recreational registration costs $30 (5 business days) or $50 expedited (2 business days). Drones over 249 g also need your home-country registration certificate.

You'll need: name, address, email, phone, drone make, model and weight, home-country registration for drones over 249 g, a colour scan of your passport photo page, intended purpose and island of operation. Operating limits: no higher than 400 ft (122 m); no further than 1,640 ft (500 m); within unaided visual line of sight; not over or within 500 ft (152 m) of an organised open-air assembly; not within 165 ft (50 m) of any person (take-off and landing no closer than 100 ft / 30 m); not over private or public property without permission; not within 16,500 ft (5,000 m) of any aerodrome or helipad; not at night or in low visibility; not in restricted or prohibited airspace.
